1934-cosmo.descEn: A simple sour can be so different with the right base spirit.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe
4. Garnish with an orange twist

2-to-2.descEn: A bittersweet cocktail that's more accessible than its ingredient list may suggest.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled glass
4. Garnish with an orange peel

20th-century.descEn: The 20th Century is a cocktail created in 1937 by a British bartender named C.A.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients with ice and shake
2. Strain into a coupe, serve up

212.descEn: The 212 is a delectable cocktail in a big, beautiful, reddish-pink package.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker and shake
2. Double strain into large, chilled glass filled with ice.
3. Optionally top with soda.
212.garnishEn: grapefruit peel or orange peel for garnish

21st-and-14-century.descEn: This twist on the 20th Century cocktail uses coconut rum as a stand-in for gin, a sub that works seamlessly with the drink's lemon and crème de cacao.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to the shaker with ice and shake to chill.
2. Strain into a glass, then garnish.

8-amaro-sazerac.descEn: Mayur Subbarao created this recipe for the opening menu at Manhattan's Amor y Amargo in 2011, and it has remained on the list there ever since.
stepsEn: Stir with ice, strain into a rocks glass pre-rinsed with Green Chartreuse, and garnish with a lemon twist.

as-kingston-negroni.descEn: A Kingston Negroni cocktail recipe that stirs the classic mix of rum, Campari and sweet vermouth with oloroso sherry and coffee beans.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Taste occasionally to ensure the coffee bean flavor has infused the drink.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish with a half orange wheel and lime twist.

absent-stars.descEn: A nouveau tropical rum cocktail with big passionfruit and grapefruit flavor.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass

absinthe-colada.descEn: Mint and coconut are an excellent pairing that's underused in cocktails.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a hurricane glass filled with crushed ice

absinthe-frappe.descEn: A dreamy classic that makes absinthe approachable and surprisingly refreshing.
stepsEn: 1. Combine syrup and absinthe in a shaker filled with ice
2. Shake for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled glass filled with crushed ice

absinthe-old-fashioned.descEn: Doug Petry of Louisville’s Rye restaurant devised this absinthe-based old fashioned.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients except bitters to a mixing glass with ice
2. Stir 20 seconds and strain into a rocks glass filled with ice
3. Dash bitters on top to layer

adonis.descEn: The cocktail was created in honor of the 1884 musical Adonis after the show reached the milestone of more than 500 shows on Broadway.
stepsEn: Stir all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

affinity.descEn: This off-the-radar classic cocktail was originally made with equal measures of Scotch whisky, dry vermouth, and sweet vermouth.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice to chill
2. Strain into a chilled glass

after-all-imperial.descEn: A fruity spin on a light, bubbly classic
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients, except sparkling wine, in a shaker and shake.
2. Strain into a collins glass or flute and top with sparkling wine.
3. Garnish with mint or rosemary
after-all-imperial.garnishEn: Sprig mint or rosemary for garnish

airmail.descEn: An endlessly drinkable sparkler of debated origin
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients except for the champagne in a mixer and shake for ten seconds
2. Strain into a flute and top with champagne

alabazam.descEn: One of the oldest sours, this drink also uses an enormous portion of Angostura bitters
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients with ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up

alaska.descEn: One of the great Chartreuse cocktails and a fundamental three-ingredient recipe
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass and stir at length, until the sides of the glass are frosty
2. Strain into a cocktail glass and serve up

alexander.descEn: The Alexander cocktail was born in London in 1922 by Hery Mc Elhone, at Ciro’s Club in honor of a famous bride, at the beginning it was called Panama, Gin was used instead of Cognac and light cocoa cream instead of dark.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker filled with ice cubes.
2. Shake and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

algonquin.descEn: Named for a historic hotel in midtown Manhattan, the classic Algonquin cocktail combines rye whiskey, vermouth and pineapple.
stepsEn: 1. Shake all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

amalfi-frappe.descEn: For this frappe, Little Rituals owner Ross Simon wanted to capture the flavors of the Amalfi Coast.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the ingredients in a glass, then add shaved ice and stir briefly to incorporate.
2. Top with more shaved ice and garnish.

amaretto-sour.descEn: Amaretto is an Italian liqueur that’s typically flavored with almonds or apricot stones.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients and, if using an egg white, dry shake
2. Add ice and shake for 10 sec
3. Strain into a glass
amaretto-sour.garnishEn: Spray aromatic bitters over foaming cocktail from atomiser and then garnish with lemon & cherry sail (lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick)

amaretto-sour-jeffrey-morgenthaler.descEn: There are two things that impede all other Amaretto Sours from challenging mine.
stepsEn: 1. Combine ingredients in a cocktail shaker and shake without ice or (even better) use an immersion blender to combine and froth.
2. Shake well with cracked ice.
3. Strain over fresh ice in an old fashioned glass
amaretto-sour-jeffrey-morgenthaler.garnishEn: Garnish with lemon peel and brandied cherries.

amaro-highball.descEn: Julep Houston bartender David Kubiak created this amaro highball to highlight Amaro Montenegro and serve as an intro to mezcal.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients, except the soda water, to a shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake and then strain into an ice-filled glass.
3. Top with the soda.

amen-corner.descEn: Created by PDT alum Nick Brown, the bourbon-based cocktail recipe is a riff on the classic Paper Plane without the lemon juice.
stepsEn: 1. Gently muddle the mint in a mixing tin.
2. Combine remaining ingredients in the mixing tin and shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with brandied cherries.

americano.descEn: The story of the Americano dates back to the second half of the 1800s in Gaspare Campari’s bar in Milan.
stepsEn: 1. Mix the ingredients directly in an old fashioned glass filled with ice cubes.
2. Add a splash of Soda Water.
3. Stir gently.
americano.garnishEn: Garnish with half orange slice and a lemon zest.

amoxicillin.descEn: Unlike the classic Penicillin, which calls for ¾ ounce honey-ginger syrup, this cocktail recipe uses yellow Chartreuse for honeyed sweetness.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients, except the peated Scotch, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Finish with six sprays of peated Scotch from an atomizer.
4. Garnish with a lemon wheel.

ancho-problem.descEn: In response to the request for "something spicy, with tequila," Ezra Star whips up this chile- and blanco tequila-spiked cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Shake all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

andalusian-buck.descEn: This drink is great because it doesn’t go too far any any direction.
stepsEn: 1. Combine gin, sherry, lime juice, and Demerara syrup in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake until cold.
3. I like to add the ginger beer directly to the shaker, then pour slowly over fresh ice in a chilled Collins glass.

angel-face.descEn: Although the origin of the cocktail is not known, the main hypotheses assume that it was born in the twenties of the twentieth century in France: this thesis would prove the presence of calvados, a liqueur commonly used in France and, in…
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker filled with ice cubes.
2. Shake and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

angie.descEn: During a visit to Panama in 2017, Bratislav Glisic, head bartender and co-founder of Dear Strangers in New York, had his first taste of maracujá, aka passion fruit.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake to chill, then strain into the glass. Garnish.
Passion Fruit SyrupCombine 1 cup of passion fruit purée and 1 cup of superfine sugar in a pot and boil. Allow to cool, then strain. Will keep in the refrigerator for 2 weeks.
angie.garnishEn: Matcha powder and dehydrated lime wheel

annas-revenge.descEn: Since Brooklyn's Bar Camillo features a range of bitter-forward cocktails, head bartender Anna Wang sought to create a lighter and refreshing alternative at Suono, the hi-fi bar below the restaurant.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake and then strain into the glass. Garnish.

apapacho-cafe.descEn: This twist on classic Irish coffee from Rosewood Mayakoba's Zapote Bar, one of the 50 Best Bars in North America, is just the thing for a chilly day.
stepsEn: 1. Pour the first 4 ingredients into the glass and gently stir. Add the whipping cream to a shaker with an ice cube and shake very hard. Strain over the cocktail, then grate the nutmeg over the top.
2. Note: The bar mixes a bit of pinole with nutmeg (4:1) for the garnish, but nutmeg alone works fine if you don’t have pinole.

apb-melrose-gin-tonic.descEn: This mesmerizingly azure-topped gin and tonic from Los Angeles' APB (A Plant Bar) Melrose draws inspiration from the state of California.
stepsEn: 1. Add the first 4 ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake until chilled, then strain into a glass over fresh ice. Add the tonic, top with pebble ice, then drizzle the blue Chareau on top. Garnish.
2. Blue ChareauAnd 1/8 tsp. of blue spirulina to 1/2 cup Chareau and whisk. Will keep in the refrigerator for 2 weeks.

aperol-spritz.descEn: A Spritz is a Venetian wine-based cocktail, commonly served as an aperitif in Northeast Italy.
stepsEn: Build all ingredients into a wine glass filled with ice. Stir gently.
aperol-spritz.garnishEn: Garnish with a slice of orange.

appetizer-a-litalienne.descEn: It could be argued that the difference between a forgotten cocktail and a beloved classic is simply the size of the audience.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a chilled glass. Express the twists over the finished cocktail, and use as a garnish.

2. Tip Schmidt didn’t specify a garnish for the drink in his 1892 book, but Yarm says a lemon twist “would smooth out the fernet’s aggression, and an orange twist to sweeten things would be nice, too.

apple-amaretto-sour.descEn: Autumn variation of Amaretto Sour by Anders
stepsEn: Shake
apple-amaretto-sour.garnishEn: Express lemon oils, add cocktail cherry

apple-kickin.descEn: A bold, lightly bitter Old Fashioned variant whose flavor profile is an intriguing blend of fresh apple alongside spiced sugarcane.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a rocks glass with a large format ice cube
2. Stir for 20 seconds

apples-all-the-way-down.descEn: A dash of bitters and fresh rosemary balance the sweetness of this bright highball that's brimming with fall fruit flavor.
stepsEn: 1. Add syrup, lemon, and brandy to a highball glass filled with ice
2. Top with cider and stir
3. Slap a sprig of rosemary to release its oils and garnish

apricot-and-coffee-highball.descEn: Apricot and coffee might not seem like an obvious flavor duo, but at Too Soon in Portland, Oregon, the idea to combine them in a cocktail came about from "wanting to explore contrast in a really approachable format," says owner/operator…
stepsEn: 1. Add the first 4 ingredients to the ice-filled glass and stir to combine.
2. Top with tonic water, then garnish.
1. Add first four ingredients to a shaker tin with ice and short shake.
2. Double strain into a wine glass over cracked clear ice and top with prosecco.
3. Garnish with red currants if you have them, lemon wedge if you don’t

archangel.descEn: A play on a Pink Gin, the Archangel cocktail recipe combines the aromatic subtlety of cucumbers, the orange of Aperol and the strength of gin.
stepsEn: 1. In a mixing glass, bruise cucumber slices with a muddler.
2. Add gin, Aperol, ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with a lemon peel.

army-navy.descEn: The Army & Navy is a tropical gin cocktail recipe made with gin, lemon juice, orgeat and Angostura bitters.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.

arrowhead-limited.descEn: Ever a lover of combining beer with bitters, Damon Boelte tops this "mezcal Negroni" cocktail recipe with IPA.
stepsEn: 1. Add Campari, mezcal and Carpano Antica to a high ball glass.
2. Add ice, and top with IPA.
3. Garnish with grapefruit slices.

arsenic-and-old-lace.descEn: The Arsenic and Old Lace is a Martini cocktail recipe made with gin, absinthe, dry vermouth, crème de violette and Angostura bitters.
stepsEn: 1. Using an atomizer, spritz a chilled coupe glass with absinthe.
2. Combine all other ingredients in a mixing glass and stir with ice.
3. Strain into prepared glass.
4. Express a lemon twist over the drink, then use as garnish.

art-of-choke.descEn: A drink that broke all the rules when Kyle Davidson first conjured it in 2008.
stepsEn: 1. Muddle mint and syrup in a mixing glass
2. Add remaining with ice and stir for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass with fresh ice

artichoke-hold.descEn: The warm funk of Smith & Cross rum creates a heavy base for the bittersweet co-mingling of amaro and elderflower in this cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add a small amount of ice and shake lightly.
3. Strain over crushed ice into a rocks glass.
4. Top with more crushed ice.

aspen-crud.descEn: Invented at Hotel Jerome during Prohibition, the Aspen Crud cocktail is a symbol of the ski town's pre-glitz history and an enduring staple.
stepsEn: 1. Add bourbon and ice cream to a blender and blitz until creamy.
2. Pour into a pint glass or Mason jar and garnish with cherries, if using. Serve with a straw.

assunta.descEn: Since every cocktail at Saint Theo's is a nod to an Italian name, ingredient, or garnish, beverage director Simon Sebbah transformed the Moscow Mule into an Italian Mule by sweetening it with amaretto.
stepsEn: 1. Add the ingredients, except the ginger beer, to a shaker with ice and shake vigorously. Pour into a highball filled with crushed ice and top with ginger beer, then garnish.

autoretrato.descEn: Autoretrato is a tropical riff on the modern classic Amaretto Sour, reinvented for a different audience.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake to emulsify the egg whites.
3. Add ice and shake until chilled.
4. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
5. Garnish with a half of passion fruit, mint leaf and a dried clover blossom.
autoretrato.garnishEn: Mint leaf, dried clover blossom, half of passion fruit

avenue-scotch.descEn: From frigid Iceland comes this tropical sour.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled Nick & Nora glass

aviation.descEn: Aviation was created in New York at the Walkick hotel by the head bartender Hugo Ensslin while he was writing his book “Recipes for Mixed Drinks” (1916) one of the last cocktail books published before the start of American Prohibition.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients into a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake with cracked ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

b-52.descEn: The origins of the B-52 are not well documented, but one claim is that the B-52 was invented by Peter Fich, a head bartender at the Banff Springs Hotel in Alberta, Canada.
stepsEn: Refrigerate ingredients then layer in chilled glass by carefully pouring in the ingredient order.

baby-turtle.descEn: A tequila cocktail recipe that combines reposado tequila, Campari, grapefruit and lime juice, cinnamon syrup and saline.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker and dry-shake (without ice) to combine.
2. Add ice to the shaker and shake until chilled.
3. Double-strain into a double Old-Fashioned glass over ice.

bacardi-cocktail.descEn: The Bacardí Cocktail was originally the same as the Daiquiri, containing rum, lime juice, and sugar; The Grenadine version of the Bacardí Cocktail originated in the US, while the original non-red Bacardí company recipe originated from Cuba.
stepsEn: Shake together with ice. Strain into glass and serve

backlash-tonic.descEn: This simple aperitivo cocktail offers layers of flavor from Melbourne's Pendant Public Bar.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a glass with a large ice cube and briefly stir to combine, and garnish.

backsliding-presbyterian.descEn: Tall and bursting with bittersweet orange and ginger flavors, this whiskey highball proves that aged spirits aren’t just for winter sipping.
stepsEn: Shake all ingredients (except club soda) with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass. Top with club soda and garnish.

bahama-mama.descEn: Tiki master Paul McGee’s recalibrated version of this classic cocktail recipe involves dialing down the proportions and sweetness.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin. Add 5 ice cubes and shake for 5 seconds.
2. Strain into a Hurricane glass filled with crushed ice.
3. Garnish with tropical fruit.

baltimore-southside.descEn: A Southside that honors the legacy of Baltimore's Black bartenders.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the rum, lemon juice, simple syrup and mint in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a double rocks glass over 1.25-inch ice cubes.
4. Top with about 1 1/2 ounces of club soda.
5. Garnish with mint and a lemon wheel.
baltimore-southside.garnishEn: mint bouquet, lemon wheel or dehydrated lemon wheel

banana-daiquiri.descEn: Popular at tropical bars and often sold in prefabricated mixes, blended versions of the classic Daiquiri rarely garner the same respect as their three-ingredient forebears.
stepsEn: 1. Put all of the ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth.
2. Pour into the chilled glass, and garnish.
banana-daiquiri.garnishEn: Three pieces of banana-shaped hard candy (optional)

barbacoa.descEn: The Barbacoa is a mezcal cocktail recipe that muddles fresh ginger syrup and lemon juice with bell peppers and Fresno chile.
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients and muddle them together.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Pour into a double Old-Fashioned glass.
4. Garnish with a piece of beef jerky.
1. Shake with pebble ice.
2. Strain into a cocktail glass.
3. Garnish.

barracuda.descEn: The Barracuda cocktail is a bright yellow Rum cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker except the Prosecco
2. Shake well with ice
3. Strain into chilled highball glass filled with ice
4. Top up with Prosecco
barracuda.garnishEn: Pineapple and Cherry, optional mint sprig for additional aroma.

basil-julep.descEn: Pick a high-character Irish Whiskey - something with rich, oily spice notes to pull down the basil's volatile peppery aroma.
stepsEn: 1. Muddle 2-3 basil leaves with gum syrup in a julep cup
2. Fill with crushed ice and add whiskey
3. Stir until cold and frosty, then top with more crushed ice

batanga.descEn: First created at a bar called La Capilla in the town of Tequila by Don Javier Delgado Corona in the 1960s, the Batanga is a favorite among fans of agave spirits.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a highball glass with ice.
2. Stir to combine.

bay-ridge.descEn: The Bay Ridge, which originated at Brooklyn cocktail lounge Clover Club around 2014, represents a long line of New York-themed cocktails based on the Manhattan.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients except garnish in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 15–20 seconds until well chilled.
3. Strain into chilled coupe or Nick & Nora glass, and garnish with an orange twist.

bebbo.descEn: The Bebbo is a cocktail recipe that riffs on the classic Bee’s Knees.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with a stripe of Angostura bitters.

bee-sting.descEn: Scotch, honey and herbal liqueurs come together in this unconventional drink from bartender Jonathan Pogash.
stepsEn: 1. Add the Bärenjäger, Laphroaig, Fernet-Branca, egg white and tangerine juice into a shaker and vigorously dry-shake (without ice).
2. Fill with ice and shake again until well-chilled.
3. Double-strain into an Old Fashioned glass filled with fresh ice.
4. Top with the bitters.

beet-it.descEn: According to Chris D'Apice, beverage director of San Diego's Books & Records, this mezcal beet cocktail drinks like an earthy, vegetal Margarita.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all of the ingredients into a shaker.
2. Add ice, give it a good shake and strain.
3. Serve up, into a coupe or martini glass.
4. Top with drops of olive oil.

**Note:** No prebottled beet juice will live up to freshly juiced beets. If you don't have your own juicer at home, the best option is to swing by your local fresh juice shop and have them make you a fresh batch. A 16-oz. to-go cup will make 16 cocktails. Natural grocery stores carry decent bottled beet juice, but they generally add acid in the form of lemon juice and citric acid as a preservative, in which case you can pull back on the amount of lime juice to keep the cocktail balanced.

bees-knees.descEn: The Bee's Knees was invented by Frank Meier, an Austrian-born, part Jewish bartender who was the first head bartender at the Ritz in Paris in 1921, when its Cafe Parisian opened its doors.
stepsEn: 1. Stir honey with lemon and orange juices until it dissolves
2. Add gin and shake with ice
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass
**Variations:**
- Barr Hill Gin is sometimes recommended for its honey infusion, though other gins may be used (including Barr Hill's Tom Cat gin).
- The honey may be diluted 1:1 with warm water to thin the consistency.
bees-knees.garnishEn: Optionally garnish with a lemon or orange zest.

belleville.descEn: At Atlanta bistro Little Sparrow, the cocktails skew classic with French accents.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and expressed lemon peel. Stir to chill, then strain over a large ice cube in the glass. Garnish with a lemon peel.

2. Note“This cocktail calls for a very under-utilized technique called the ‘Royal Stir’ where we incorporate a lemon peel in the mixing glass to gently add brightness and texture during the stir—but not getting in the way of the aromatics of the final cocktail via an expression. We encourage home bartenders to experiment with this approach if they want to highlight the high quality of the spirits that are being used rather than the citrus garnish.”—Allison Lovelace

bellini.descEn: The Bellini was invented sometime between 1934 and 1948 by Giuseppe Cipriani, founder of Harry's Bar in Venice, Italy.
stepsEn: 1. Pour peach puree into the mixing glass with ice
2. Add the Prosecco wine.
3. Stir gently and pour in a chilled flute glass.

bentons-old-fashioned.descEn: The Benton’s Old-Fashioned cocktail recipe is the drink that introduced the concept of “fat-washing” spirits to the cocktail world.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice (preferably a large cube).
4. Garnish with an orange peel.

beton.descEn: The Beton is a Czech cocktail starring Becherovka, an herbal liqueur, and tonic water, that is sometimes compared to a Gin and Tonic.
stepsEn: 1. Add ingredients to a highball glass with ice.
2. Garnish with a lemon slice.

betty-carter.descEn: Most whiskey and bourbon-based cocktails are synonymous with the cold time of the year, when one turns to the warming qualities of these spirits.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
betty-carter.garnishEn: Garnish with an orange twist and a sprig of mint.

betty-is-back.descEn: Named for the Connaught Bar's head bartender during the 1940s, this sparkler was the first cocktail on the famed bar's menu when it reopened in 2008.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients, except the Champagne, in a mixing glass filled with ice and stir until well chilled. Strain into a flute and gently pour in the Champagne. Garnish.

between-the-sheets.descEn: The origin of the cocktail is usually credited to Harry MacElhone at Harry's New York Bar in Paris in the 1930s as a derivative of the sidecar.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients into a cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass

beuser-angus-special.descEn: Chartreuse sour from Berlin, the Beuser & Angus Special takes inspiration from the Last Word and the Ramos Gin Fizz.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first five ingredients in a cocktail shaker and shake hard with ice.
2. Strain into a rocks glass filled with ice.
3. Top with orange flower water.

bijou.descEn: This cocktail was invented by Harry Johnson, "the father of professional bartending", who called it bijou because it combined the colors of three jewels: gin for diamond, vermouth for ruby, and chartreuse for emerald.
stepsEn: Stir in mixing glass with ice and strain

bijou-blanc.descEn: A modern take on the Bijou, this cocktail recipe puts a fresh spin on the classic Chartreuse cocktail, similar to a White Negroni.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with a lemon peel “flag.”

bitter-giuseppe.descEn: First featured on an early menu at the Violet Hour in Chicago, Stephen Cole's Bitter Giuseppe cocktail has become a modern classic over the years, with iterations popping up on menus at places like Cure in New Orleans, Elske and Ludlow…
stepsEn: 1. Stir all the ingredients together in a mixing glass with ice until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube and garnish.

bitter-mai-tai.descEn: Perhaps the most riffed-upon cocktail in the tiki canon, the Mai Tai cocktail recipe serves as the inspiration for this bitter spin.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients in a cocktail shaker. Add ice and shake until chilled, about 10 seconds.
2. Strain into a large rocks glass over crushed ice.
3. Garnish with mint sprig.

black-manhattan.descEn: Amaro Averna stands in for sweet vermouth in this Manhattan-inspired modern classic cocktail recipe from Todd Smith.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with a cherry.

black-russian.descEn: Variations: **WHITE RUSSIAN** – Float fresh cream on the top and stir in slowly.
stepsEn: Pour the ingredients into the old fashioned glass filled with ice cubes. Stir gently.

black-walnut-old-fashioned.descEn: If you are after an Old Fashioned riff with a warming complexity then a Walnut Old Fashioned should hit the spot.
stepsEn: Combine ingredients in a mixing glass with ice. Stir until chilled. Strain into an Old Fashioned glass with fresh ice.
1. Muddle berries, mint, and syrup in a mixing tin
2. Add lemon juice, whiskey and ice
3. Shake until chilled
4. Double strain over crushed ice into a rocks glass

blackthorn.descEn: With roots dating back to 19th-century New Orleans, the Blackthorn cocktail is one of the few classics to highlight Irish whiskey.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a glass filled with fresh ice, and garnish.

blinker.descEn: Calling on a full ounce of grenadine to complement the grapefruit juice and rye base, this cocktail recipe is potent but refreshing.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients except the grapefruit twist in a cocktail shaker filled with ice and shake until chilled, about 15 seconds.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Twist a piece of grapefruit zest over the drink and drop into the glass.

blood-and-sand.descEn: An exceptionally smooth classic with an optional smoky finish
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients with ice and shake
2. Strain into a coupe
3. Flame orange peel and garnish

blood-moon.descEn: The Blood Moon cocktail recipe is just one example of Joe Campanale's ode to aperitivo, on the menu at Alta Linea.
stepsEn: 1. Build in a wine glass over ice and garnish with a orange half-moon

bloody-caesar.descEn: The Bloody Caesar is a clam-juice-spiked riff on the Bloody Mary.
stepsEn: 1. Coat the rim of a tall glass with celery salt, fill with ice and set aside.
2. Add the vodka, Clamato juice, Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco and horseradish into a mixing glass with ice.
3. Pour back and forth into another mixing glass a few times to combine.
4. Strain into the prepared glass.
5. Garnish with a celery stalk, cucumber spear and lime wedge.

bloody-mary.descEn: If requested served with ice, pour into highball glass.
stepsEn: Stir gently all the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice, pour into rocks glass.
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a shaker with ice and shake vigorously.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Express a lemon peel and use as a garnish.

blue-hawaii.descEn: Adapted from a recipe created in 1957 by Harry K.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker tin.
2. Flash-blend for 4 to 5 seconds with 4 ounces of crushed ice.
3. Pour into a hurricane glass over 8 ounces of crushed ice.
4. Garnish with sliced pineapple, pineapple fronds and an orchid.

bluebird-eggnog.descEn: This eggnog cocktail recipe from Baltimore bar The Bluebird combines cream, rum, apple brandy, an egg and simple syrup.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and dry-shake vigorously.
2. Add ice, and quickly hard-shake.
3. Double-strain into a rocks glass with light ice.
4. To garnish, place a white chocolate eggshell on top of the cocktail.
