bon-soiree.descEn: This cocktail from Hailey Knight and Casey Knight (no relation) of Charleston's Félix Cocktails et Cuisine takes the spicy Margarita for an extra-savory spin.
stepsEn: 1. Rim a chilled glass with tajin.
2. Combine the ingredients in a shaker with ice.
3. Shake to chill, then strain into the prepared glass.

boothby.descEn: Proof that tinkering with classic cocktails is an evergreen endeavor, the Boothby is a pre-Prohibition Manhattan variant with an effervescent crown.
stepsEn: 1. In an ice-filled mixing glass, combine the first four ingredients and stir to chill. Strain into a chilled coupe and top with sparkling wine. Garnish with the skewered cherry.

boozy-shakerato.descEn: Perfect for an after dinner pick-me-up or a morning wake-up call, this boozy shakerato recipe is as versatile as it is delicious.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the simple syrup, espresso and your choice of either limoncello, sambuca, or amaretto in shaker and fill with ice. Shake vigorously to create a fully aerated, fluffy drink. Strain into an after-dinner glass.

boulevardier.descEn: The boulevardier is similar to a Negroni, sharing two of its three ingredients.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
boulevardier.garnishEn: Garnish with orange zest, optionally a lemon zest.

bourbon-lift.descEn: The cocktail equivalent of a New York egg cream, this rich and fizzy bourbon drink is absolutely delicious.
stepsEn: 1. Add the bourbon, coffee liqueur, heavy cream and orgeat into a shaker and vigorously dry-shake (without ice) for 10 seconds. Add ice and shake again until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a Collins glass.
3. Fill with the club soda, pouring from about 6 inches above the glass.
4. Wait a few seconds and then add another splash of soda. This will lift the foam above the top of the glass.
5. Serve with a straw.

bourbon-renewal.descEn: This one was named after a band that my business partner, Tony Figoli was in a long time ago.
stepsEn: 1. Shake ingredients with ice until cold.
2. Strain over fresh ice into an old-fashioned glass.
3. Garnish with a lemon wedge, or if in season, fresh currants.
bourbon-renewal.garnishEn: Garnish with a lemon wedge, or if in season, fresh currants

bourbon-stone-sour.descEn: A refreshing bourbon cocktail designed for summer, combining citrus fruitiness with the spirit's notes of oak, vanilla, and caramel.
stepsEn: 1. Combine bourbon, fresh orange juice, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over fresh ice.
bourbon-stone-sour.garnishEn: Orange slice, mint sprig, cocktail cherry

brainstorm.descEn: This classic Irish whiskey cocktail from Hugo Ensslin’s 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks has been adapted for contemporary use, with the French vermouth and honeyed herbal liqueur Bénédictine given greater billing in the glass.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a chilled glass.
2. Twist an orange peel over the cocktail and use as garnish.

bramble.descEn: The Bramble was created in London, in 1984, by Dick Bradsell.
stepsEn: If crème de mûre is unavailable, many bartenders will substitute creme de cassis for it.
1. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker except the Crème de Mûre
2. Shake well with ice
3. Strain into chilled old fashioned glass filled with crushed ice
4. Pour the blackberry liqueur (Crème de Mûre) over the top of the drink, in a circular motion.
bramble.garnishEn: Garnish optionally with a lemon slice and blackberries.

brandy-crusta.descEn: The cocktail, named for the crust of sugar on the rim, was invented by Joseph Santini, a bartender in New Orleans at his bar, Jewel of the South.
stepsEn: Mix together all ingredients with ice cubes in a mixing glass and strain into prepared slim cocktail glass.
brandy-crusta.garnishEn: Rub a slice of orange (or lemon) around the rim of the glass and dip it in pulverized white sugar, so that the sugar will adhere to the edge of the glass. Carefully curling place the orange/lemon peel around the inside of the glass.

brasserie-special.descEn: Bring a bottle of whiskey to the island with this passionfruit-based sour.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe

breakfast-margarita.descEn: There are several takes on the Breakfast Margarita, a Marg inspired by Salvatore Calabrese's Breakfast Martini.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake to chill.
2. Fine strain into a glass over fresh ice.
3. Garnish.

breakfast-martini.descEn: This cocktail recipe is one of the earliest—and still the most famous—examples of jam as an ingredient in a cocktail revival era.
stepsEn: 1. Stir the marmalade with the lemon juice at the bottom of a cocktail shaker until it dissolves.
2. Add the gin and Curaçao. Shake with ice. Fine strain into a chilled cocktail coupe.
3. Shred some orange peel on the top of the drink as a garnish.

bright-orchard-gin-and-tonic.descEn: A refreshing winter variation of the classic gin and tonic that combines orchard fruits, citrus, and juniper notes.
stepsEn: 1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Pour in the gin, apple juice, and lemon juice.
3. Top with light tonic water.
4. Stir once to integrate.
5. Garnish with an apple slice and rosemary sprig.

brown-bomber.descEn: Similar to white negroni but built with whiskey
stepsEn: Stir all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

brown-derby.descEn: The Brown Derby cocktail, a classic bourbon drink, was named for the famous Los Angeles diner and is both sweet and sour.
stepsEn: 1. Add the ingredients into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Fine-strain into a cocktail glass.
3. Express the oil from a grapefruit twist over the drink and drop the twist into the drink to garnish.

bywater.descEn: The Bywater is a rum and Chartreuse cocktail recipe from New Orleans that riffs on the Brooklyn, itself a Manhattan riff.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all ingredients until chilled in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Strain into a coupe or a Nick & Nora glass.
3. Express an orange twist over the surface, then discard. Garnish with a cherry.

cable-car.descEn: Tony Abou-Ganim, also known as The Modern Mixologist, is a bartending legend that co-founded the Starlight Room.
stepsEn: 1. Start with rimming your cocktail glass with cinnamon and sugar!
2. Put your glass to the side and add ice to your shaker.
3. Add all the ingredients.
4. Shake cold!
5. Strain into your rimmed cocktail glass.
6. Serve!

cafe-ireland.descEn: Likening this cocktail to a dry Irish whiskey Manhattan, Yanni Kehagiaras notes that the drinkshould be stirred very briefly with ice.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients with ice and stir very briefly, only for 5 seconds or so. Strain into the glass and serve.

cafe-martini.descEn: At Saint Theo's in New York, beverage director Simon Sebbah elevates the Espresso Martini by trading out vodka for reposado tequila, giving it "a little extra kick and dimension."
stepsEn: 1. Add all the ingredients to a shaker with ice
2. Shake and strain into the glass

cafe-racer.descEn: A cold weather appropriate digestif, inspired by the delicious pairing of cacao, coffee, and raw cane sugar.
stepsEn: 1. Add ingredients to a mixing glass with ice
2. Stir 20 seconds and strain into a chilled glass
3. Express an orange peel and garnish

caipirinha.descEn: Although the origin of the drink is unknown, one account says it came about around 1918 in the region of Alentejo in Portugal, with a popular recipe made with lemon, garlic, and honey, indicated for patients with the Spanish flu.
stepsEn: 1. Place lime and sugar into a double old fashioned glass and muddle gently.
2. Fill the glass with cracked ice and add Cachaça.
3. Stir gently to involve ingredients.

calvados-tonic.descEn: The Calvados & Tonic is a staple in Normandy.
stepsEn: 1. Pour the Calvados into a Burgundy glass over ice.
2. Top with tonic water.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

calypso.descEn: Named for the ship belonging to French ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau, this tropical port cocktail—combining rum from Barbados, tawny Port from Portugal, and bergamot liqueur from Italy—showcases the fortified wine's summery side.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker, add ice, then shake vigorously. Double-strain into a rocks glass with a large cube, then garnish.

cameron-park-spritz.descEn: Named after a Hispanic neighborhood in Brownsville, Texas, this Spritz incorporates flavors that nod to that heritage, says Christopher Galicia, beverage director and junior partner with Ramblas Hospitality Group.
stepsEn: 1. Add the Aperol, elderflower liqueur, and mezcal to an ice-filled glass. Add a splash of sparkling water, then top with 2-3 oz. of sparkling wine. Garnish.
Combine all in wine glass

campbeltown.descEn: Three ingredients add up to one perfect sip in this expensive and utterly delicious Scottish cocktail
stepsEn: 1. Add the Springbank 10-year-old scotch, Cherry Heering liqueur, and green Chartreuse into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled Nick & Nora glass.
3. Express the oil of a lemon peel over the drink and discard.

canchanchara.descEn: Known as the forerunner of the Daiquiri, and drunk by Cuban revolutionaries fighting off the Spanish at the end of the nineteenth century, the Canchànchara is a simple mix of honey, citrus and rum (originally aguardiente de caña rather…
stepsEn: Mix honey with water and lime juice and spread the mixture on the bottom and sides of the glass. Add cracked ice, and then the rum. End by energetically stirring from bottom to top.

cane-tables-royal-hawaiian.descEn: A tropical gin cocktail recipe, the Royal Hawaiian is reimagined at Cane & Table, where the pineapple drink is served on crushed ice.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker.
2. Add a handful of pebble ice and whip-shake.
3. Pour into a chilled double rocks glass, and top with more pebble ice.
4. Garnish with a mint bouquet and serve with a straw.

cantaritos.descEn: Cantaritos are Mexican tequila cocktails served in clay cups!
stepsEn: 1. If using the traditional clay cup for serving, soak it in cold water for 10 minutes before using. Otherwise, use a highball glass.
2. Combine the tequila, orange juice, lemon juice and lime juice in the glass with a pinch of salt.
3. Fill the glass with ice and top with grapefruit soda.

carajillo.descEn: Bolstering one’s coffee with a shot of booze is more or less a universally accepted practice, regardless of time of day or occasion.
stepsEn: 1. Brew 3 oz. of espresso per drink and cool to room temperature or chill in

the fridge to prevent excess dilution. In a shaker filled with ice, add chilled espresso and Licor 43. Shake well until creamy and frothy, then strain into the glass filled with fresh ice, and garnish.
TIPThe Carajillo is as much a coffee drink as it is a cocktail—brewing the espresso fresh, and using a high-quality coffee, will have a big impact on the final flavor.

cardinale.descEn: In Dale DeGroff’s revised and updated The New Craft of the Cocktail, he details the backstory of the Cardinale cocktail, a 1950’s-era variation on the classic Negroni.
stepsEn: Stir the gin, Campari, and vermouth with ice in an Old Fashioned glass, then garnish.

caribbean-ember.descEn: Tyler Malone of Zasu New Orleans wanted to create a rum cocktail with depth and warmth, one that bridges the gap between Old Fashioned-style cocktails and tropical drinks—"two worlds that don't often meet," he says.
stepsEn: 1. Add the ingredients, except the ginger beer, with ice in a shaker. Shake and strain over fresh ice in a glass. Top with ginger beer. Garnish.

caribbean-ember-2.descEn: Tiki cocktails and whiskey is far from traditional cocktail combination.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients except ginger beer in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass filled with ice.
4. Top with chilled ginger beer.
caribbean-ember-2.garnishEn: Garnish with a sprig of mint, lime wheel, pineapple spears and an edible flower.

caribbean-parachute.descEn: This rum and tonic adds the building blocks of a Silver Fizz and the balance of a rich amaro, resulting in a beautifully textured highball.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients except tonic water to a shaker with no ice.
2. Shake to combine, then add ice and shake well until chilled and foamy.
3. Add chilled tonic water to an empty Collins glass, then strain the cocktail into the tonic until the top of the drink is half an inch below the rim.
4. Wait for the foam to completely settle, then finish straining the remainder of the cocktail.

casino.descEn: This version of the Casino Cocktail first appears in 1909, in The Reminder (3rd edition) by Jacob A.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into cocktails shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled rocks glass with ice.
casino.garnishEn: Garnish with lemon zest and a maraschino cherry.

ce-soir.descEn: A mix of Cognac, with touches of yellow Chartreuse and Cynar, and two types of bitters, this cocktail recipe is potent and elegant.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
3. Express the lemon peel and discard.
Muddle the celery with the lemon juice and simple, then shake with the gin and ice.

central-park-to-lumphini.descEn: Tantai Khantachavana of BKK New York, a restaurant that blends Bangkok street food and New York cuisine, deliciously encapsulates the experience of an autumn stroll in his fig cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake to chill and dump into a glass over a large ice cube. Garnish.

champagne-cocktail.descEn: A recipe for the cocktail appears as early as "Professor" Jerry Thomas' Bon Vivant's Companion (1862), which omits the brandy or cognac and is considered to be the "classic" American version.
stepsEn: Place the sugar cube with 2 dashes of bitters in a large Champagne glass, add the cognac. Pour gently chilled Champagne.
champagne-cocktail.garnishEn: Garnish with orange zest and maraschino cherry.

charles-dickens-punch.descEn: “Dickens was a dedicated punch-maker and an inveterate showman,” says drinks historian David Wondrich, offering as proof this historic flaming punch from his 2010 book Punch: The Delights (and Dangers) of the Flowing Bowl.
stepsEn: 1. A few hours before preparing the punch, peel 4 lemons with a vegetable peeler or paring knife to create 4 long spirals of peel. Put them in a heatproof bowl with 3/4 of a cup of demerara sugar. Muddle the peels and
the sugar together and let sit at room temperature. Juice the 4 peeled lemons (and any extra needed) through a strainer to yield 6 oz. of strained juice. Set aside in the fridge.

2. Measure the rum and Cognac into a pitcher or other pouring vessel. To prepare the punch, boil the water and place the bowl containing the lemon peels and sugar on a wooden cutting board or other heat-resistant surface in an open area (free from clutter, flammable items, or nearby curtains or light fixtures) where everyone can gather around at a safe distance.

3. Pour the Cognac and rum into the bowl. Use a long-handled barspoon to remove a spoonful of the rum-cognac mixture. Light the spoonful on fire with a match and hold it just above the surface of the bowl in order to ignite the rest of the liquid. Stir with the barspoon or a heatproof ladle to help dissolve the sugar. Let the mixture burn for 2 or 3 minutes, occasionally lifting out one of the lemon peels with the ladle or spoon to show the flames running down it.

4. Cover the bowl with a large heatproof dish or tray to extinguish the flames. Add the lemon juice and the hot water. (For cold punch, replace the hot water with 3 cups of cold water and add a 1-quart block of ice, made by freezing a quart bowl of water for 24 hours.) Stir. Grate fresh nutmeg over the top and ladle out in 3-ounce servings.

chauncey.descEn: Equal-parts gin, Cognac and rye whiskey with sweet vermouth and orange bitters make up this historic cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with a lemon or orange twist.

chocolate-martica.descEn: This simple variation on a Death & Co modern classic from 2007 was one of the first to tap chocolate bitters’ flavor potential.
stepsEn: Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a chilled glass.

chrysanthemum.descEn: Hard to spell but easy to drink, the Chrysanthemum falls into the category of lesser-known classics—still held in good regard, but not often invited to the party.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice until chilled. Strain into a chilled glass and garnish.

2. Tip“I would also try this with blanc vermouth, as many of the recipes of this era like the Algonquin, El Presidente, and Blackthorn that call for dry vermouth taste better with blanc vermouth, in my opinion,” notes Meehan.

ciderhouse-mule.descEn: Taking the Moscow Mule into spritz territory, Tim Sweeney, head bartender of Pebble Bar in New York City, combines vodka, lime, and ginger syrup with a touch of raspberry liqueur and sparkling rosé.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients, except the sparkling rosé, to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake until chilled.
3. Add the sparkling rosé to the shaker before straining the cocktail into a glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish.

cinder-bloom.descEn: "The inspiration behind this cocktail began with my love for the Margarita," says Omar Bautista, beverage manager of Boro Brine in New York City.
stepsEn: 1. Place 4 ají dulce peppers in a shaker and muddle. Add the rest of the ingredients along with ice. Shake hard for about 5 seconds, or until the outside of the shaker is frosty. Strain into the glass over ice.

clarified-new-york-sour.descEn: This clarified take on the New York Sour achieves a silky mouthfeel and a softened acidity, making for an easy-drinking sipper.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the bourbon, lemon, and simple syrup and pour over the milk in a glass container.
2. Let sit for 30 minutes, allowing the milk to curdle.
3. Strain the milk mixture through a coffee filter.
4. If it’s not clear, re-pour through the same filter.
5. To serve, pour the mixture over a large ice cube in a glass.
6. Float with red wine.

clover-club.descEn: The Clover Club Cocktail is a drink that pre-dates Prohibition in the United States, and is named for the Philadelphia men's club of the same name, which met in the Bellevue-Stratford Hotel at South Broad and Walnut Streets in Center City.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into cocktails shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.
The egg white is not added for the purpose of giving the drink flavor, but rather acts as an emulsifier. Thus when the drink is shaken a characteristic foamy head is formed.

clover-leaf.descEn: This recipe from James Beard Award-winning culinary historian and journalist Toni Tipton-Martin is a modern take on a century-old relative of the Clover Club cocktail, utilizing a base of gin and Chambord to create a berry-forward delight.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the Chambord or grenadine, lemon juice, egg white or half-and-half, and gin in a cocktail shaker with ice cubes.
2. Shake vigorously for 10 seconds, until the ingredients are cold and the mix is frothy with a pink blush.
3. Strain into a Martini or coupe cocktail glass, making sure there is a thin layer of foam and a few small ice chips floating on top.
4. Garnish with the mint leaf.

coffee-cigarettes.descEn: The Coffee & Cigarettes cocktail was created by Thomas Waugh and featured in the Death & Co.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the ingredients into your mixing glass
2. Stir with ice for 30-40 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled stemmed cocktail glass

coffee-cocktail.descEn: It probably would be difficult to come up with a more misleading name for this cocktail, than Coffee Cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake to emulsify the egg.
3. Add ice and shake until chilled.
4. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
coffee-cocktail.garnishEn: Garnish with some freshly grated nutmeg.

coffee-enzoni.descEn: The Enzoni is a personal favorite of mine.
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker, muddle the grapes
2. Add the remaining ingredients
3. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
4. Double strain over ice into an old fashioned glass
5. Garnish with 3 skewered black grapes

coffee-julep.descEn: Coffee liqueur and Demerara Gum Syrup give this Julep a jolt of rich flavor.
stepsEn: 1. Muddle 5-10 mint leaves with syrup in a julep cup
2. Fill with crushed ice and add bourbon and coffee liqueur
3. Stir until cold and frosty, then top with more crushed ice
4. Smack a mint sprig between your hands to express its oils, then garnish

coffee-negroni.descEn: It’s commonly been said that the only thing better than a Negroni is a Coffee Negroni.
stepsEn: Stir all ingredients in an ice-filled mixing glass, then strain into an ice-filled rocks glass

comte-de-sureau.descEn: The name translates to count of elderflower, which is a nod to the St-Germain that acts as the floral sweetener here.
stepsEn: Stir with ice and strain into a chilled rocks glass over ice.
comte-de-sureau.garnishEn: Garnish with orange and lemon twists.

conference-cocktail.descEn: Tiki was jealous of the Old Fashioned build, and the Conference cocktail was born.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice
2. Stir 20 seconds and strain into a chilled rocks glass with ice.

coronado-cocktail.descEn: The combination of Tropical Passionfruit Syrup, coconut water, and tequila has tropical written all over it.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a highball glass over crushed ice
4. Garnish with a lemon wheel

corpse-reviver-2.descEn: The Corpse Reviver №2 as described in the Savoy Cocktail Book is the most commonly drunk of the corpse revivers, and consists of equal parts gin, lemon juice, curaçao (commonly Cointreau), Kina Lillet (now usually replaced with Cocchi…
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into shaker with ice. Shake well and strain in chilled cocktail glass.

cosa-nostra-2.descEn: A delicious and simple Highball created by Dane Barca at Smuggler's Cove
stepsEn: Shake everything except the ginger ale with ice and strain into a pilsner glass over crushed ice.
Top with the ginger ale

cosmopolitan.descEn: A cosmopolitan, or informally a cosmo, is a relative of cranberry coolers.
stepsEn: Add all ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice. Shake well and strain into a large cocktail glass.

countermand.descEn: The Countermand is a mini reverse Martini cocktail recipe served at the NYC restaurant Somssi.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a chilled, petite glass with one large ice cube.
2. Stir briefly, then express a lemon coin over the drink and discard.

creole-gimlet.descEn: Falernum adds hints of Caribbean Island flavors for a tasty twist on the classic Gimlet.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and shake.
2. Double strain into a chilled Coupe glass.
3. Garnish with lime wheel.

cuba-libre.descEn: The cocktail originated in the early 20th century in Cuba, after the country won independence in the Spanish–American War.
stepsEn: Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
Combine all ingredients and shake with ice. Serve in a rocks glass over crushed ice. Garnish with a rolled cucumber slice.

cynar-flip.descEn: A magnificent application of Cynar in the holiday canon
stepsEn: 1. Dry shake the whole egg in a cocktail shaker
2. Add Cynar, simple syrup, and ice before shaking again
3. Strain into a cocktail glass and drop several dashes of the bitters into the foam

daiquiri.descEn: Daiquirí is also the name of a beach and an iron mine near Santiago de Cuba, and is a word of Taíno origin.
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker add all ingredients.
2. Stir well to dissolve the sugar.
3. Add ice and shake.
4. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

daiquiri-4.descEn: A frozen Daiquiri cocktail recipe from Cafe La Trova, also known as the Hemingway Daiquiri, after the author who was known to drink them.
stepsEn: 1. Blend all ingredients with a scoop of crushed ice for 15 seconds.
2. Pour into an 8 1/2-ounce coupe glass.
3. Serve with straws.

dantes-garibaldi.descEn: The flagship drink at Dante is named after Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Garibaldi, who was a central figure in the unification of Italy.
stepsEn: 1. Build the Campari and orange juice in a small highball glass filled with ice.
2. Stir and garnish with the orange wedge.

dark-n-stormy.descEn: This drink is very similar to the Moscow mule except that the Dark 'n' Stormy has dark rum instead of vodka.
stepsEn: In a highball glass filled with ice pour the ginger beer and top floating with the Rum.
dark-n-stormy.garnishEn: Garnish with a lime wedge or slice.

day-o-fashioned.descEn: The Day-O’ Fashioned is a tropical Old-Fashioned cocktail recipe made with rye whiskey, rum, banana liqueur, cold brew, orange and Angostura.
stepsEn: 1. In a rocks glass, muddle the orange peel with the bitters.
2. Add the rest of the ingredients and ice, and stir gently until well-chilled.
3. Garnish with an orange slice and a black cherry.

dead-mans-handle.descEn: This summery tequila cocktail from Tiffany Kirk at Miss Carousel in Houston gets punched up with Aperol and perfectly sweetened with orgeat.
stepsEn: Combine, Shake with Ice. Top with a sprinkle of Tajín seasoning.

dead-sea-mule.descEn: A house-made pomegranate grenadine is the key to the Dead Sea Mule, a mezcal-laced twist on the classic Moscow Mule.
stepsEn: 1. Fill a Collins glass with ice, then add the mezcal, lime juice and grenadine.
2. Top with the ginger beer and stir briefly and gently to combine.
3. Garnish with the mint sprig and 2 skewered pieces of candied ginger.

death-flip.descEn: When this cocktail first appeared on the menu at the Black Pearl in Melbourne, in 2010, no ingredients were listed.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice. Strain into a sour glass.

debbie-dont.descEn: An adventurous modern cocktail for those with a limited bar
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up

deep-south.descEn: Our peach syrup, with a split base of mezcal and rye whiskey, adds a summer note to this whiskey sour.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass

delta-t.descEn: A cocktail designed to highlight the unique buttery and funky notes of Variable Dunderclap rum, balanced by the sharpness of ginger and the herbaceous qualities of Fernet.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients except ginger beer to a shaking tin.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a highball glass over an ice spear.
4. Top with ginger beer.
5. Add several dashes of Angostura bitters on top.
delta-t.garnishEn: candied ginger, lime peel, and a fresh bunch of mint

diki-diki.descEn: A revived golden-era cocktail and fabulous way to tinker with Swedish Punsch
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up

dirty-martini.descEn: The Dirty Martini is a popular cocktail that adds olive brine to the classic Martini, giving it a savory flavor.
stepsEn: 1. Select and pre-chill a Martini glass.
2. Prepare garnish of skewered Green Olives.
3. Stir all ingredients with ice.
4. Strain into chilled glass.
5. Garnish with skewered olives.

disgruntled-mai-tai.descEn: The Disgruntled Mai Tai is a spin on the rum tiki drink that adds Aperol and a bottle of bitter Underberg to the cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients except for the Underberg in a cocktail shaker.
2. Briefly dry shake without ice, then add a few small ice cubes and shake until the ice has melted.
3. Pour into a chilled rocks glass and top with crushed ice.
4. Remove the cap and the top of the paper wrapper on the Underberg bottle and insert it, upside-down, into the crushed ice.
5. Garnish with a mint sprig, lime wedge, grated nutmeg and a cocktail umbrella.
disgruntled-mai-tai.garnishEn: mint sprig, lime wedge, freshly grated nutmeg, cocktail umbrella

division-bell.descEn: Mezcal takes the place of gin and Aperol that of Chartreuse in this simple riff on the Last Word.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a coupe.
3. Express a grapefruit twist over the surface of the drink, then discard.

don-lockwood.descEn: A chocolate, smoky riff on the old fashioned that proves simple variations on classic cocktails can have impressive results.
stepsEn: 1. In a mixing glass combine all ingredients
2. Stir with ice for 20-30 seconds
3. Strain over ice into an old fashioned glass

dons-mai-tai.descEn: Don’s Mai Tai is a tiki cocktail recipe originally from Don the Beachcomber.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Dump into a double rocks glass and top with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a brandied cherry, lime wedge and mint bouquet.
dons-mai-tai.garnishEn: brandied cherry, lime wedge, fresh mint

doubleplusgood.descEn: Doubleplusgood is Boston barman John Gertsen’s take on a Mai Tai, crossed with a Pisco Sour.
stepsEn: Dry-shake all ingredients (except the bitters) first without ice, then again with ice added. Double-strain through a fine mesh strainer into a chilled short glass, no ice. Drop the bitters atop the foam in the shape of two plus symbols.
doubleplusgood.garnishEn: two plus signs, drawn in the foam with aromatic bitters

dreamy-dorini-smoking-martini.descEn: This Vodka Martini riff from Audrey Saunders is anything but ordinary, with peaty single malt scotch and Pernod taking the place of dry vermouth and orange bitters.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a cocktail glass.
3. Express the oils from the lemon twist over the drink, then garnish with the twist.

drifter.descEn: At ABV in San Francisco, the concept is simple: The menu is built around the spirits that the owners want to drink, and the drinks they want to make from them.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir gently.
2. Strain into a double rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with a grapefruit twist.

drunk-uncle.descEn: Drunk Uncle is a cocktail inspired by a negroni, specifically a scotch negroni, with bold, strong bitter-sweet and boozy taste profile.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir for 30-45 sec. or approx. 60 revolutions.
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
drunk-uncle.garnishEn: Garnish with a twist of grapefruit.

e-tonico.descEn: E Tonico is a Gin & Tonic with an Italian twist courtesy of an aperitivo liqueur, vermouth and saline solution.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first five ingredients in a Collins glass and fill with ice.
2. Top with tonic water.
3. Garnish with a bay leaf.

eastside.descEn: The Eastside is a gin-based cocktail recipe that was created by George Delgado at Libation in New York City, New York.
stepsEn: 1. Add three cucumbers slices and mint leaves to a shaker.
2. Muddle gently for 5-7 seconds.
3. Add gin, lime juice, simple syrup, and cubed ice to shaker.
4. Shake for 10-20 seconds.
5. Fine strain into a cocktail glass.
eastside.garnishEn: Garnish with remaining cucumber slice and mint sprig.

eel-bars-marianito.descEn: This Marianito cocktail recipe swaps the typical gin for rum, specifically an agricole rhum.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice, then garnish with an olive on a pick and an orange twist.

eeyores-requiem.descEn: Three bitter amari, including Fernet-Branca, get amped up with aromatic French vermouth and juniper-rich gin in this cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
3. Express three orange twists over the surface of the drink, discarding the first two and saving the third for garnish.

eggnog.descEn: An archetypal example of a traditional eggnog recipe with farm-fresh dairy and a blend of whiskey, rum and Cognac.
stepsEn: 1. Separate the eggs.
2. Whisk the yolks and sugar together until they firm up and their bright orange color fades to a more opaque pale yellow.
3. Slowly add the spirits, milk and cream while continuing to whisk air into the batch.
4. Beat the egg whites and salt together to stiff peaks.
5. Whisk the egg whites into the mixture.
6. Bottle and store in the refrigerator until chilled, the longer the better.

el-abuelo.descEn: This Old Fashioned-inspired cocktail by Carolina González of Chicago's Trino adds warmth and depth to the whiskey cocktail using the earthy herbaceousness of a Mexican amaro and the baking spices of a spiced brown nectar.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir for approximately 10 seconds.
2. Strain over a large ice cube into the glass.
3. Garnish.
el-abuelo.garnishEn: Sprig of thyme and an orange swath

el-gibson.descEn: "In the spring, we went hard on spring onions at the farmers market, and pickled them,” says John Douglass of Imbibe 75 Place to Watch, Pretty Decent in Louisville, Kentucky.
stepsEn: 1. Place the pickled onion wedge in a chilled Nick & Nora glass. In a mixing glass, stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into the prepared glass.

2. Pickled Spring OnionsThoroughly wash a bunch of spring onions, and use a knife to remove all of the green parts. Cut the onions into wedges, maintaining the root end (to hold the onion together). Pack the onions into a sanitized canning jar or a large food-safe plastic storage container.

3. In a pot, combine a mixture of 60 percent water and 40 percent champagne vinegar (the quantity will depend on the size of the batch you’re preparing). Weigh this liquid mixture and add 5 percent of its weight in sugar, and 3 percent of its weight in salt. Add several bay leaves, 1 Tbsp. of black peppercorns, and 1 Tbsp. of coriander seeds, and bring the mixture to a boil, whisking to dissolve the sugar.
4. Once the mixture is boiling, remove it from the heat and pour it over the onions, to cover. Cover the container and let it cool; will keep refrigerated for up to 1 month.

el-pepe.descEn: Although A16’s El Pepe cocktail recipe looks innocent in a glass, it’s delightfully complex, built with a structure similar to Margarita.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over a large rock into a rocks glass.
4. Garnish with a basil leaf.

el-presidente.descEn: The El Presidente earned its acclaim in Havana during the 1920s through the 1940s during the American Prohibition.
stepsEn: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
Stir everything with ice, strain to glass.

electric-current-fizz.descEn: The Electric Current Fizz is an easy cocktail recipe that pairs a gin fizz with a prairie oyster, a dressed egg yolk shot.
stepsEn: 1. In a shaker, combine all ingredients except for soda water. Add one small piece of ice and shake until the ice is dissolved; this helps emulsify the egg white.
2. Add more ice to the shaker and hard shake, then strain into a fizz glass or short Collins glass.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Serve the fizz with the prairie oyster in a shot glass.
### Prairie Oyster

Reserve the egg yolk, taking care not to puncture it. Season the yolk with a pinch of salt, black pepper and Worcestershire sauce and Tabasco to taste (start with one dash of each). Serve in a shot glass alongside the drink.
electric-current-fizz.garnishEn: Prairie Oyster in a shot glass

employees-onlys-mezcal-margarita.descEn: Steve Schneider, principal bartender at New York’s Employees Only, has a long history with Margaritas.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a shaker, and add ice.
2. Shake until chilled and strain into ice-filled tumbler glass.

endless-summer.descEn: Yanni Kehagiaras riffs on the Negroni cocktail recipe with Campari, gin, sweet vermouth, and an ounce of pineapple.
stepsEn: 1. In a large shaking tin, add all ingredients. Add ice, and shake well.
2. Fine strain into a Collins glass over ice.
## Editors note:
This drink can easily be scaled up into a large-format cocktail; for guidelines, see <a href="https://punchdrink.com/articles/five-batched-summer-cocktails-recipes/">here</a>.

english-garden.descEn: The English Garden brings together some classic pairings for St-Germain Elderflower liqueur - gin, apple, lime & cucumber.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Strain over fresh ice into a high ball

enzo.descEn: The Enzo is an Americano cocktail made with a Ferrari, the 50/50 shot of fernet amaro and Campari.
stepsEn: 1. Add the first three ingredients to a Collins or highball glass over ice.
2. Top with soda water and garnish with an orange peel or a half-slice.

enzoni.descEn: The Enzoni Cocktail is a true modern classic that will impress your guests!
stepsEn: Muddle grapes, add ingredients, shake then double strain. Garnish with more green grapes on a cocktail pick.

eponine-collins.descEn: A French-inflected Collins cocktail recipe from Sarah Morrissey builds on a base of gin, complemented by Suze and Amaro Montenegro.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a collins glass over ice and top with soda.
3. Garnish with two cucumber slices and two basil leaves.

eric-alperins-tuxedo-no-2.descEn: This variation on the Tuxedo cocktail recipe—a sherry-spiked Martini—dates to the turn of the 20th century and swaps sherry for dry vermouth.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients, except absinthe, in a mixing glass over cracked ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe rinsed or atomized with absinthe.
3. Express lemon twist, then use as garnish. Finish off with a brandied cherry.

espresso-martini.descEn: It is not a true martini as it contains neither gin nor vermouth, but is one of many drinks that incorporate the term martini into their names.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.

fairy-sugar-momma.descEn: As much as I liked the hint of anise in a corpse reviver I never was one to eat a black jelly bean on its own.
stepsEn: Shake ingredients

fancy-free.descEn: The Fancy Free is a variation on the Old-Fashioned.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled double rocks glass over a big cube.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

femme-fatale.descEn: Rather than serving sparkling wine alongside their Pornstar Martini variation, Austin's The Long Goodbye adds it directly to the glass.
stepsEn: 1. Pour the sparkling wine into a chilled coupe. Shake the remaining ingredients and fine strain into the coupe. Optional: Shake hibiscus dust on the surface of the cocktail and swirl with a barspoon.

Passion Fruit Vanilla SyrupIf using frozen purée, thaw 2 1/4 oz. of passion fruit purée (Long Goodbye uses Perfect Purée) completely and bring to room temperature. Add 2 1/4 oz. of granulated sugar and 1/3 tsp. of vanilla syrup and whisk to combine completely. Refrigerate to store. Makes approximately 6 servings and will keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Hibiscus DustUsing a spice grinder, pulse 1/4 cup of dried hibiscus flowers to a fine powder. Store in a shaker. Makes approximately 6 servings.

fernandito.descEn: The cocktail first became popular among the youth of the college town of Córdoba, in the 1980s and—impulsed by an advertising campaign led by Fratelli Branca—its consumption grew in popularity during the following decades to become…
stepsEn: Pour the Fernet Branca into a double old fashioned glass with ice, fill the glass up with Cola. Gently stir.

ferrari.descEn: The Ferrari cocktail recipe, a potent 50/50 split of Fernet-Branca and Campari, can be taken as a shot or sipped slowly.
stepsEn: 1. Combine and drink as a shot.

final-ward.descEn: The Final Ward is perhaps the best-know riff on the classic Last Word and was created in 2007 by Phil Ward at Death & Co.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass
final-ward.garnishEn: Cocktail cherry at the bottom of the glass

fiore-di-francia.descEn: In this cocktail recipe Italian amaro, Cynar, joins forces with St-Germain in a nod to the border zone where elderflower grows freely.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients in a mixing glass, add ice and stir.
2. Strain into a coupe.
3. Express the lemon peel and discard.

first-frost.descEn: Even though carrots are available year round, Isai Xolapa, beverage director of W Philadelphia's Living Room, wanted to celebrate how the veggie can lend an earthy warmth and a natural sweetness to cocktails.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously until well chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish.

five-point-palm-exploding-heart-techniqu.descEn: This smoky, bittersweet cocktail combines mezcal’s earthy intensity with the bitter depth of Punt e Mes and the richness of coffee liqueur.
stepsEn: 1. In a mixing glass, combine the ingredients
2. Stir until chilled
3. Strain over ice into a rocks glass

flannel-shirt.descEn: Bartender Jeffrey Morgenthaler of the Clyde Common in Portland, Oregon, created the Flannel Shirt for an autumnal event.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel.

floppydisk.descEn: The tricky thing when it comes to low ABV drinks is that the end result doesn’t always give that same feeling of a proper mixed drink.
stepsEn: Shake without soda

floradora.descEn: A little spice and a burst of berry flavor - this highball is perfect for a sunny afternoon.
stepsEn: 1. Short shake all ingredients except soda water
2. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice
3. Top with soda water and stir.
1. Stir all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into chilled glass.
for-mezcalicus-sake.garnishEn: Express lime zest twist over cocktail and use as garnish.

stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe

french-75.descEn: The drink dates to World War I, and an early form was created in 1915 at the New York Bar in Paris—later Harry's New York Bar—by barman Harry MacElhone.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all the ingredients, except Champagne, into a shaker.
2. Shake well and strain into a Champagne flute.
3. Top up with Champagne.
4. Stir gently.

french-connection.descEn: The cocktail is named for the Gene Hackman film of the same name.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients directly into an old fashioned glass filled with ice cubes. Stir gently.

french-gimlet.descEn: A simple 3-ingredient riff on a classic Gimlet.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass

french-martini.descEn: It was invented in the 1980s at one of Keith McNally's New York City bars.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.
french-martini.garnishEn: Squeeze oil from lemon peel onto the drink.

french-pearl.descEn: This cocktail recipe puts gin and pastis in the same shaken drink—along with lime juice, simple syrup and mint leaves.
stepsEn: 1. In a shaker tin, add the lime juice, simple syrup and mint then muddle.
2. Add the gin, pastis and ice and shake until chilled.
3. Fine strain into a coupe.

french-pearl-2.descEn: This refreshing, elegant libation is a tribute to the Beaux-Arts Neoclassical architectural movement of the late 1800s in France, an era in which sipping pastis was quite fashionable.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the lime juice, cane syrup, and mint sprig in a cocktail shaker.
2. Muddle the ingredients.
3. Next, add the Pernod and gin.
4. Fill the shaker to the top with ice and shake well.
5. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

frozen-margarita.descEn: A frozen Margarita cocktail recipe made with tequila, Cointreau, fresh lime and orange juices and raw agave.
stepsEn: 1. Prepare the glass, if using the lime-salt rim. Moisten half the rim of a double rocks glass with a lime wheel, then dip gently in kosher salt.
2. Combine all ingredients in a blender.
3. Fill a 13-ounce double rocks glass with a heaping scoop of pebble ice (see Editor’s Note).
4. Add ice to the blender and blend until smooth.
5. Pour into a double rocks glass.
frozen-margarita.garnishEn: lime and kosher salt rim, optional

stepsEn: 1. In a blender jug, combine all the ingredients
2. Blend until smooth
3. Served in a tall glass

fumata-bianca.descEn: This cocktail recipe is a soft, yet edgy mixture of sweet blanca vermouth, herbal Suze, and smoky mezcal that goes down easy.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients except the grapefruit twist in a collins glass.
2. Add ice and top with club soda.
3. Express a grapefruit twist over the drink and drop into the glass.

garibaldi-spritz.descEn: This version of the classic Garibaldi cocktail recipe dials back the Campari and tops all with prosecco, turning the classic into a spritz.
stepsEn: 1. To an ice-filled Collins glass, add the Campari and orange juice and stir to combine.
2. Top with prosecco and garnish.

gaz-regans-negroni.descEn: In Gaz Regan's nontraditional take on the classic Negroni cocktail recipe, Jägermeister stands in for Campari.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.

gemist.descEn: Coming from a german word "gemischt", meaning mixed.
stepsEn: Combine cold ingredients in a glass.
Ingredient amounts are usually eyeballed depending on the glass.

gentlemans-exchange.descEn: A strong rocks cocktail with an emphasis on coffee and bourbon
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients except the grapefruit peel in a mixing glass and stir for about ten seconds
2. Pour into a rocks glass over a large cube and garnish with the grapefruit peel

getaway-car.descEn: Meaghan Dorman's take on the Jungle Bird cocktail recipe swaps in Ancho Reyes for Campari—alongside a kick of ancho chili powder.
stepsEn: 1. Fill a shaker tin half-full with pebble ice.
2. Add all ingredients and shake.
3. Fill a Zombie mug half-full with pebble ice.
4. Strain into the mug, and garnish with a lime wheel and a sprinkle of ancho powder.
getaway-car.garnishEn: lime wheel and a sprinkle of ancho powder

ghost-coast.descEn: An unforgettable tour of western America in cocktail form
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice and garnish
ghost-coast.garnishEn: eucalyptus leaf and/or banana chip for garnish

gibson.descEn: More fun than answering who first plopped a pickled pearl onion—instead of an olive, or a lemon twist—into a dry gin Martini is recalling who didn’t.
stepsEn: 1. Stir the ingredients with ice to chill, then strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
2. Garnish with the pickled pearl onion.

gimlet.descEn: The word "gimlet" used in this sense is first attested in 1928.
stepsEn: 1. Add gin, lime juice, and syrup to a cocktail shaker. Fill with ice and shake until cold.
2. Strain into glass and top with a splash of soda water, if desired.

gin-it.descEn: The Gin & It is a classic cocktail recipe made with London dry gin, sweet vermouth, Angostura bitters.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain into a glass on the rocks.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

gin-tonic.descEn: Called a “G and T” or gin tonic in some countries, this refreshing drink is made in countries all around the world.
stepsEn: 1. Add lots of ice to a large cocktail or wine glass and stir to chill the glass. Drain any melted water.
2. Pour in the gin. Add the garnishes. Pour the tonic water onto a bar spoon into the glass (to increase the bubbles). Stir once and serve.
gin-tonic.garnishEn: Any of the following to spice your cocktail: Lime, lemon, cucumber, mint, orange peel, juniper berries, blood orange slice, rosemary

gin-basil-smash.descEn: At Le Lion where the drink was created in 2008, 300 to 500 have been sold every week since its debut—22,000 a year—and the bar goes through more than 3,100 bottles of gin every twelve months.
stepsEn: 1. Muddle basil leaves in a shaker tin.
2. Add remaining ingredients and ice and shake until chilled.
3. Double strain into a rocks glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with basil leaves.

gin-blossom.descEn: The Gin Blossom is Julie Reiner's (of Brooklyn's Clover Club) modern play on the classic Martini cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice, and stir to chill.
3. Strain into a coupe glass and garnish with an expressed orange peel.

gin-daisy-new-school.descEn: This cocktail recipe is a variation on the basic Daisy formula: a sour kicked up with the addition of seltzer or soda water.
stepsEn: 1. Add gin, lemon juice, grenadine and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a Collins glass.
4. Garnish with a slice of orange.

gin-fizz.descEn: A gin fizz is the best-known cocktail in the fizz family.
stepsEn: 1. Shake all ingredients with ice except soda water.
2. Pour into thin tall Tumbler glass
3. Top with a splash soda water
4. Serve without ice
gin-fizz.garnishEn: Garnish with a lemon slice, optional lemon zest.

gin-pahit.descEn: An easy cocktail recipe from Malaysia.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Nick & Nora glass, then garnish with the lemon twist on the rim of the glass.

gin-rickey.descEn: Andra "AJ" Johnson created this juicy, aromatic Gin Rickey cocktail recipe while consulting for a Mediterranean restaurant.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a highball glass over ice.
3. Top with club soda.
4. Garnish with straw, lemon and lime ribbons and fresh basil.
gin-rickey.garnishEn: straw, lemon and lime ribbons, fresh basil

gin-gin-mule.descEn: This cocktail recipe is essentially a Mojito (a rum drink) crossed with a Moscow Mule (a vodka drink), but made with gin.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the lime juice, syrup and mint in a mixing glass and muddle.
2. Add the gin and ginger beer and ice and shake well.
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with mint leaves

giving-basil.descEn: Gabe Fountain, lead bartender of Oklahoma City's The Jones Assembly, took the classic Gimlet, added an herbaceous complexity with Italicus liqueur and basil, then rounded out the flavors and texture with pistachio orgeat for an…
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake, then double strain into a chilled glass.
3. Spritz with the vanilla tincture, then garnish.
giving-basil.garnishEn: Small basil leaf or dried basil blossom

go-to.descEn: Created by Rob Krueger, Extra Fancy, Brooklyn NY.He mentioned this to a guest one night, to which she responded, "Oh, so it's your go-to?" inspiring the cocktail's name.
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients except the ginger beer
2. Shake briefly with ice to combine
3. Strain over ice into a highball glass
4. Top with ginger beer
go-to.garnishEn: Garnish with a mint sprig and cucumber wheels

godfather.descEn: The Godfather cocktail is a simple Scotch and amaretto drink that’s full of flavor!
stepsEn: 1. Add the blended scotch and amaretto to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain the drink into a lowball glass and fill it with ice. (To take it over the top, add a splash of single malt scotch on top).

godfather-iv.descEn: A riff on the amaretto-sweetened Godfather cocktail recipe, this drink adds on walnut liqueur for extra depth and nutty richness.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

going-out-west.descEn: This smoky sipper is the perfect Wild West-ish twist on the Old Fashioned, featuring rye whiskey, mezcal for a touch of smoke, and Averna amaro for depth.
stepsEn: 1. Add rye whiskey, mezcal, amaro, and simple syrup to a mixing glass.
2. Add a good amount of ice and string for 20-30 seconds.
3. Strain into an old fashioned glass with a large cube.
4. Get an orange peel, squeeze it to express oils, and throw the garnish into the glass.

gold-rush.descEn: Created at famed New York City bar Milk & Honey in the early 2000s, this drink's combination of bourbon, lemon and honey became worldwide modern classic.
stepsEn: 1. Add the bourbon, honey syrup, and lemon juice into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over one large ice cube.

golden-dream.descEn: The Golden Dream was popular during the 60s and 70s and originated at the Old King Bar in Miami, mixed by Raimundo Alvarez.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into shaker filled with ice. Shake briskly for few seconds. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

good-christian-pear.descEn: David Burnette, South on Main, Little Rock, Arkansas
stepsEn: 1. Shake with ice
2. Double-strain into a coupe.
good-christian-pear.garnishEn: Garnish with a pear slice or lemon wheel.

gram-arita.descEn: A Cadillac Margarita served at the Copper Room in Yucca Valley made with reposado tequila, Grand Marnier and lime juice.
stepsEn: 1. Rim half of a glass with salt and set aside.
2. Combine first three ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the prepared glass over ice.
4. Float Grand Marnier on top.

grand-armys-amaretto-sour.descEn: This Amaretto Sour cocktail recipe from New York bar Grand Army combines Campari, amaretto, lemon juice and an egg white.
stepsEn: 1. Combine ingredients in a cocktail shaker and dry-shake without ice.
2. Add ice and shake again until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass.
4. Express an orange twist over the drink, then discard.

grand-collins.descEn: A riff on a Tom Collins, the Grand Collins playfully swaps out Old Tom Gin for Grand Marnier, creating an intriguing, layered flavour profile to match its lively effervescence.
stepsEn: Place ice cubes in a highball glass and add Grand Marnier®, and then fresh lemon juice. Top up with soda water and stir.

grapefruit-reviver.descEn: For this take on the Brown Derby, bartender James Sauer of Louisville's North of Bourbon leans into its grapefruit flavor with Malört.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake to chill. Strain into the glass. Garnish.

grasshopper.descEn: A Grasshopper is a sweet, mint-flavored, after-dinner drink.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake briskly for few seconds.
3. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

grasshopper-blanco.descEn: Liz Kelley, lead bartender at Cure in New Orleans, created this twist on the Grasshopper that uses blanco tequila to help cut through the drink's sweetness.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker.
2. Add ice and hard shake to incorporate the cream and chill.
3. Double strain into the glass.
3. Garnish.

green-eyes.descEn: Chartreuse ups the herbacousness of this gin cocktail from bartender Andrew Volk.
stepsEn: 1. Dry-shake all ingredients without ice to combine, then add ice and shake again until chilled and foamy.
2. Double-strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice; garnish.

harvard.descEn: A brandy twist on a Manhattan that stands out with seltzer

heart-of-stone.descEn: Stuart Weaver, general manager and partner of Denver's Lady Jane, says this Boulevardier variation was the result of a last-minute menu change at the bar, quickly coming together 30 minutes before service began.
