pink-lady.descEn: A tart, silken drink from the 1930s.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Fill with ice and shake for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe

pisco-sour.descEn: A pisco sour is an alcoholic cocktail of Peruvian origin that is typical of the cuisines from Peru.
stepsEn: Add all ingredients into a shaker with ice.
Shake and strain into a chilled goblet glass.
pisco-sour.garnishEn: Few dashes of Amargo or Angostura bitters on top as an aromatic garnish.

pina-colada.descEn: The name piña colada (Spanish) literally means "strained pineapple", a reference to the freshly pressed and strained pineapple juice used in the drink's preparation.
stepsEn: Blend all the ingredients with ice in an electric blender, pour into a large glass, and serve with straws.
**Note:**
Historically a few drops of fresh lime juice were added to taste. 4 slices of fresh pineapple can be used instead of juice
pina-colada.garnishEn: Garnish with a slice of pineapple with a cocktail cherry.

pina-verde.descEn: This Piña Colada riff relies on Green Chartreuse rather than rum.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into rocks glass over pebble ice.
3. Garnish with a mint sprig.

planters-punch.descEn: The cocktail has been said to have originated at the Planters Hotel in Charleston, South Carolina, but actually originated in Jamaica.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients directly in a small tumbler or a typical terracotta glass.
NOTE:
Add dilution up to taste, it can be given by water, ice or juices.

poached-pear.descEn: It turns out the flavors of a classic French dessert, the red wine poached pear, work beautifully as a fall/winter cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients except for the spiced wine syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake until the shaker is cold and frosty, about 10-15 seconds.
3. Strain into a large rocks glass with fresh ice.
4. Add the spiced wine syrup by sinking it to the bottom of the glass.

poets-dream.descEn: Manhattan’s Lantern’s Keep adapted this poetic sipper from a 1930s English bar guide.
stepsEn: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass and stir with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish.

poolside-gossip.descEn: Inspired by summertime memories and photographer Slim Aaron's iconic midcentury "Poolside Gossip" photo, Alicia Perry, beverage director of San Diego hospitality group CH Projects created this sessionable spritz.
stepsEn: 1. Add 1 strawberry to a shaker and muddle.
2. Add the remaining ingredients, except the sparkling wine, to the shaker.
3. Shake with ice, strain into an ice-filled glass.
4. Top with sparkling wine.
5. Garnish.
Lemongrass Vodka:

poppas-pride.descEn: Made with Buck and a Whiskey Smash, this ginger-laced bourbon drink is one of Brooklyn bartender Jay Zimmerman's signature cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Add bourbon, ginger juice, lemon wedges and mint to cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a highball or Collins glass over fresh ice.
4. Top with soda water and Angostura bitters (don't be shy about the bitters).
5. Garnish with a mint sprig.

porn-star-martini.descEn: This easy passion fruit cocktail is bursting with zingy flavours and is perfect for celebrating with friends.
stepsEn: 1. Scoop the seeds from one of the passion fruits into the glass of a cocktail shaker
2. Add the vodka, passoa, lime juice and sugar syrup.
3. Add a handful of ice and shake well
4. Strain into a martini glass
5. Serve with shot of chilled Champagne on the side
porn-star-martini.garnishEn: Half a passion fruit on top

port-light.descEn: In the Trader Vic’s tradition, this drink is served in a Port Light glass, which resembles a rounded lantern with red glass and gold trim; the same glass in green is called a Starboard Light glass.
stepsEn: Shake with ice, Dump

porto-flip.descEn: The Porto Flip was first recorded by Jerry Thomas in his 1862 book The Bartender’s Guide: How to Mix Drinks; A Bon Vivant’s Companion.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

poseidon.descEn: The Poseidon served at Crevette in New York is quite different from the sweet blue ’tinis and fizzes floating around the internet with the same name.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with a lemon peel and olive on a pick.

pousse-cafe.descEn: A pousse-café is now a term for any multi-layered cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. In a small decorative flute or Pousse Café glass, build the first five ingredients in order. (The ingredients will naturally layer themselves on top of or right under the previous one, depending on density.)
pousse-cafe.garnishEn: Express a lemon twist over the drink and discard.

prado.descEn: The Prado is a sophisticated tequila sour that redefines the classic egg white cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake to emulsify the egg whites.
3. Add ice and shake until chilled.
4. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
5. Garnish with a lime wheel, skewered cherry, and a small sprig of mint.
prado.garnishEn: Lime wheel, skewered cherry, small sprig of mint

prime-inspector.descEn: Winter is a high time for strong, boozy stir-down cocktails and Prime Inspector is a perfect candidate for that.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir for 30-45 seconds.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish with an orange twist and a cherry.

prince-charles-dont-surf.descEn: A riff on the Army & Navy cocktail, this San Diego sipper adds gin and citrus to an orgeat-rich highball topped with beer.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients except beer, and shake with ice.
2. Strain into an ice-filled glass, top with beer and garnish.

puebla-york.descEn: Imbibe 75 Person to Watch and Puebla-born bartender Victor Lopez celebrates Mexican flavors through his cocktails at New York City's Mixteca, featuring unique twists on classics.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir to chill and strain into the glass.
3. Garnish.

puritan.descEn: The Puritan is a Martini that's similar to an Alaska.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a Martini glass and garnish with a lemon twist.

queen-of-the-rodeo.descEn: This "gussied-up" Cosmo recipe replaces Cointreau and cranberry juice for a mix of grenadine, maraschino liqueur, and grapefruit juice.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker along with ice and shake. Strain into a chilled glass. Garnish.
queen-of-the-rodeo.garnishEn: Lime wheel, a dusting of edible pink glitter (optional)

stepsEn: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

queens-park-swizzle.descEn: An old school island drink with a beautiful presentation
stepsEn: 1. In a tall glass, gently muddle mint leaves with simple syrup and lime juice
2. Add rum and top with crushed ice
3. Swizzle briefly to mix until glass frosts
4. Add more crushed ice, top with bitters and sprig of mint

quilty.descEn: In this spirit-forward cocktail recipe, smoky whisky, mezcal, nutty amontillado sherry and bittersweet coffee liqueur are paired together.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a double rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with lemon peel.

rabbit-szn.descEn: Blanco tequila, lime juice, ginger syrup and a float of sweet vermouth make up this bubbly, easy cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Add the first three ingredients to a shaker and whip-shake with a few ice cubes.
2. Strain into a Collins glass.
3. Top with club soda, add ice, then float sweet vermouth on top.
4. Garnish with a sprig of mint.

rabo-de-galo.descEn: Rabo de Galo is a classic cocktail made of cachaça, sweet vermouth and Cynar from Brazil.
stepsEn: 1. Pour the cachaça, vermouth and Cynar into a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass with ice.
3. Garnish with a lime twist.

rainy-day-fund.descEn: While working on her own White Negroni riff, Courtney McKamey—Weather Up's beverage director—ran into a road block.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a glass, add ice, and stir to chill. Garnish.

rainy-day-fund-2.descEn: While working on her own White Negroni riff, Courtney McKamey—Weather Up's beverage director—ran into a road block.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a glass, add ice, and stir to chill. Garnish.

ramos-fizz.descEn: Created by New Orleans bar owner Henry C.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients except soda water in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake for two minutes.
3. Double strain in a glass.
4. Pour the drink back in the shaker, and hard shake without ice for one minute.
5. Strain into a highball glass, top up with soda.
Or, if using blender:

ranglum.descEn: The Ranglum was invented by bartender Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro in Berlin in the aughts and has since become a known entity at craft cocktail bars across Germany.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into an ice-filled rocks glass.
3. Garnish with a lime wedge.

rattlesnake.descEn: The Rattlesnake is a classic whiskey cocktail recipe combining rye, absinthe, lemon juice, simple syrup and an egg white.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and dry shake, without ice.
2. Add ice and shake again until chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a coupe glass.
rattlesnake.garnishEn: Garnish with an Angostura bitters swirl.

reading-nook.descEn: The type of coffee used greatly impacts the flavor of this spirit-free coffee drink from 2025 Imbibe 75er Morgan Eckroth.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker and dry shake vigorously for 45 seconds.
2. Add ice and shake again for 15 to 30 seconds to fully chill.
3. Strain into the glass.
4. Express orange oil atop the drink before serving.
5. Garnish.

real-charmers-daiquiri.descEn: The nuclear Daiquiri cocktail recipe served at Los Angeles bar Real Charmer combines rum, green Chartreuse, coconut syrup and lime juice.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients in a shaker and hard shake with ice.
2. Double-strain into Nick and Nora glass.

red-hook.descEn: This contemporary Manhattan riff is a balanced people-pleaser
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients over ice and stir
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up

red-morning-light.descEn: Smoky scotch and bittersweet Campari combine for the perfect cold-weather sipper from Vegas.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice until chilled.
2. Strain into a glass holding a large ice cube.
3. Use an atomizer to spray the drink with a smoky scotch, then garnish. (Alternately, drip several drops of scotch atop the drink, then garnish.)

remember-the-alimony.descEn: A split base of fino sherry and Cynar are finished with a measure of gin for a thoroughly modern sherry cocktail recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all the ingredients except the orange twist in a rocks glass filled with one large piece of ice.
2. Stir until chilled, about 30 seconds.
3. Express an orange twist over the drink and drop into the glass.

remember-the-maine.descEn: This rye-based cocktail recipe has an ingredient list that’s part Sazerac, part Manhattan and has a grandiose backstory to boot.
stepsEn: 1. In a chilled coupe or cocktail glass, add a dash of absinthe. Roll around to coat and discard excess.
2. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
3. Add ice and stir well.
4. Strain into prepared coupe or cocktail glass.
5. Garnish with a brandied cherry.

reno.descEn: The story which inspired this cocktail took place during WWII on 21st April 1945, when the allied forces planned to retake Bologna.
stepsEn: 1. Throw all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into over a large cube ice.
3. Garnish.

revolver.descEn: A San Francisco original, and an exceptional coffee-laced riff on the Manhattan
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients over ice and stir around 15 seconds
2. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish

rib-tickler.descEn: Created by Alex Day, Nitecap, NYC.This drink was born out of the idea to create a more sippable, bubbly White Negroni (which is Suze, gin, and Lillet Blanc or blanc vermouth).
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all ingredients
2. Shake briefly with ice to combine
3. Strain over ice into a wine glass
4. Top with soda water

ric-pear-blanc.descEn: Wine-based cocktails are the primary stock-in-trade at Sacramento bar and restaurant Ro Sham Beaux, and this drink accents blanc vermouth’s floral, fruity characteristics with the flavors of pear and ginger.
stepsEn: 1. Shake all of the ingredients without ice until foamy, then add ice to the shaker and shake again until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled glass, and garnish.

risorgimento-ditalia.descEn: A more spiritous twist on the Garibaldi cocktail recipe, this drink sees additions of gin and absinthe to the orange juice and Campari.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first four ingredients in a Collins glass, then stir and add spear ice (or cubes).
2. Using an atomizer, spritz the absinthe over the top of the drink.
3. Garnish with an orange slice sprinkled with salt.

ritz-cocktail.descEn: Dale DeGroff raised the cocktail flag over New York during his tenure at the Rainbow Room in the 1980s and '90s.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first 4 ingredients in a shaker and fill with ice. Shake well to chill, then strain into a chilled glass. Top with Champagne and garnish.

rob-roy-no-3.descEn: Brian Silva's overhaul of a classic scotch whisky cocktail recipe is inspired by the structure of a "perfect" cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel.

rocinante.descEn: Named after Don Quixote's horse, this mezcal sipper blends "smoky, bitter, floral, and sweet notes that tell a story of exploration and timeless landscapes," says Aaron Sanchez of Denver's Lady Jane cocktail bar.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir and strain over a large cube in a glass.
3. Garnish.
Add arugula into your shaking tin, add ice, and shake for 10 seconds. Add remaining ingredients, shake until chilled. Double strain into chilled glass over fresh ice.

roman-holiday.descEn: Jungle Bird is a quintessential tiki / tropical cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Fill a cocktail shaker with gin, Amaro, Campari, pineapple juice, lime juice, and cold brew coffee. Add ice to the shaker.
2. Shake well until the mixture is chilled.
3. Fill a glass with crushed ice.
4. Strain the cocktail over the crushed ice.
5. Garnish with pineapple leaves and a cinnamon stick that's been charred on the edge with a lighter or blowtorch. Serve the cocktail immediately.

rome-with-a-view.descEn: Michael McIlroy's Rome With a View cocktail recipe falls somewhere between an afternoon appropriate Collins and an Americano.
stepsEn: 1. Add Campari, dry vermouth, lime juice and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a Collins glass.
4. Top with soda water and garnish with an orange wheel.

room-key.descEn: It’s basically a Skeleton Key with white rum instead of whiskey.
stepsEn: Shake on ice and pour into a Collins glass over ice. Top with Mineral Water and then add all the angostura dashes to the top. Serve with a straw.

rubino-tequila-spritz.descEn: “The intention behind the Rubino Spritz was to bridge the gap between the palates and desires of our Knoxville audience and our authentic northern Italian brand,” explains Madison Walker, bar manager at Brother Wolf.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first 3 ingredients in a shaker with ice. Shake and strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice. Top with blood orange soda and Prosecco, then garnish.

rum-and-ramazzotti.descEn: This cocktail is an interesting take on the classic Jungle Bird, drawing inspiration from this well-known tiki drink with a couple of key substitutions.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over fresh pebble ice.
4. Garnish with a few lime wheels, skewered cherry and pineapple spears.

rum-old-fashioned.descEn: The oldest recipe for this cocktail appeared in cocktail guides around 1860 and called for it to be made with gin.
stepsEn: Add all ingredients to a stirring glass, fill with ice, stir and strain.

russian-spring-punch.descEn: The Russian Spring Punch was created in London, England by Dick Bradsell in the 1980s.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker except the sparkling wine, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled tall tumbler glass filled with ice, and top up with sparkling wine.
russian-spring-punch.garnishEn: Garnish with blackberries and optionally a lemon slice as well.

rusty-nail.descEn: A Rusty Nail can be served in an old-fashioned glass on the rocks, or "up" in a stemmed glass.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients directly into an old fashioned glass filled with ice. Stir gently.

rusty-ringo.descEn: From New York's Bar Goto, a modern interpretation of the Rusty Nail cocktail recipe made with calvados, Scotch and Drambuie liqueur.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir for 60 rotations.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with gold leaf.

sage-gibson.descEn: Gary Wallach, partner of Lindens NYC, infuses vodka with one of his favorite herbs, sage, for his take on the Gibson cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir to chill. Add the onion and sage to a chilled glass. Pour the cocktail into the glass.
Sage-Infused VodkaAllow fresh sage (roughly 1 leafy sprig per 8 oz) to steep and infuse vodka for 3 days.
sage-gibson.garnishEn: Pickled onion and fresh sage leaf

saisonniere.descEn: The winter version of Lafayette's seasonally changing staple cocktail recipe—hence, the name Saisonnière—is an herbal riff on the basic sour.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a sage leaf and a lemon twist.
saisonniere.garnishEn: sage leaf and a lemon twist

sakura-martini.descEn: Bar Goto's Martini cocktail recipe combines salted cherry blossom with maraschino and the dry, vinous quality of sake.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a glass and garnish with a salted cherry blossom.

salmoncito.descEn: This bittersweet, citrusy highball made with gin, Campari, grapefruit and tonic is a Mexico City-born modern classic.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first three ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
2. Top with tonic water.
3. Garnish with a supremed grapefruit wedge and a grapefruit twist; express oil from the grapefruit peel and then discard it.
salmoncito.garnishEn: A supremed grapefruit wedge and a discarded grapefruit twist

sang-amer.descEn: For something light to whet the appetite, mix together this tequila aperitif cocktail from Chemin à la Mer in New Orleans.
stepsEn: 1. Reverse dry shake (shake hard with ice first and then remove the ice and shake hard again) to achieve a frothy layer. Pour into an ice-filled glass. Garnish.

sangria.descEn: A punch, sangria traditionally consists of red wine and chopped fruit, often with other ingredients or spirits.
stepsEn: 1. Chop the orange (leaving the peel on) and apple into bite-sized chunks, then add them to the bottom of a pitcher. Sprinkle them with sugar and stir. Let them stand for 20 minutes at room temperature.
2. After 20 minutes, pour in the red wine, brandy, orange liqueur, and lemon rounds. Stir and refrigerate 1 to 4 hours. (Don’t go beyond 4 hours or the fruit texture starts to degrade.)
3. Pour the sangria into ice filled glasses and top with a splash of sparkling water (if desired). Add fruit to each glass, preferably on long skewers for easy snacking.
sangria.garnishEn: Drop fruit chunks into a glass

saturn.descEn: Winner of 1967's International Bartender's Association World Cocktail Championship - The Saturn is ready for its comeback!
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice

sauvignon-blanc-punch.descEn: This vibrant white wine meets its perfect match, Aperol, in Alex Day’s epic punch recipe.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients except the club soda into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a highball glass filled with fresh ice.
3. Top with the club soda and stir briefly and gently to combine.

savoy-special-1.descEn: For those who find martinis overly dry, this variation incorporates a hint of grenadine to craft a smoother and well-balanced flavor profile.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice
2. Stir 20 seconds and strain into a chilled martini glass

sawyer.descEn: The Sawyer, a cocktail recipe from Ssäm Bar, is an icy, bitters-soaked twist on a gimlet doctored with nearly thirty dashes of bitters.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass.

sazerac.descEn: The Sazerac is a local variation of a cognac or whiskey cocktail originally from New Orleans, named for the Sazerac de Forge et Fils brand of cognac brandy that served as its original main ingredient.
stepsEn: 1. Rinse a chilled old-fashioned glass with the absinthe.
2. Add crushed ice and set it aside.
3. Stir the remaining ingredients over ice in a mixing glass.
4. Discard the ice and any excess absinthe from the prepared glass.
5. Strain the mixed drink into the glass.

scofflaw.descEn: The creatively named Scofflaw combines whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice and grenadine.
stepsEn: 1. Add the whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice, grenadine and orange bitters into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

scorched-earth.descEn: A wild and daring twist on the Negroni
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass and stir
2. Strain into a lowball or whiskey glass over ice
3. Flame orange peel (optionally) and garnish

scorpion-bowl.descEn: The Scorpion, like many tiki cocktails, has gone through countless iterations, from a gin and wine-laced libation to this contemporary version of Trader Vic’s 1946 recipe (even he prescribes several riffs in his own books).
stepsEn: 1. Put everything in a blender.
2. Blend for up to 10 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a Tiki bowl.

scorpion-reef.descEn: The Scorpion Reef is a creation of Marshall Davis from the Gallo Pelón Mezcaleria.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients except the Angostura bitters
2. Half fill with crushed / pebble ice
3. Swizzle until glass is frosted
4. Finish with Angostura bitters and five spice

scotch-and-coconut.descEn: A split base of rum and Scotch might sound like the perfect match for cold-weather sipping, but when curaçao and coconut water enter the equation, the combo takes a turn for the tropical.
stepsEn: 1. A day ahead of making the cocktail, freeze the coconut water in a large ice cube mold.
2. When ready to make the drink, combine the ingredients in a shaker with ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over the frozen coconut water ice.

scotch-sling.descEn: The Improved Scotch Sling is a sour cocktail recipe that gets stirred, rather than shaken.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with a lemon peel.

screwdriver.descEn: A screwdriver is a simple and popular alcoholic highball drink made with orange juice and vodka.
stepsEn: 1. Add ice to tumbler glass first.
2. Add vodka and orange juice next
screwdriver.garnishEn: Garnish with slice of orange or homemade orange twists

sea-breeze.descEn: The cocktail is usually consumed during summer months.
stepsEn: Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
sea-breeze.garnishEn: Garnish with orange zest and cherry

sea-legs.descEn: The Sea Legs cocktail encapsulates "a nautical feel without the kitsch", says its creator Alejandro Olivares.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a Hybrid Cocktail Shaker.
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
sea-legs.garnishEn: Garnish with a salted rim and lime wheel.

second-serve.descEn: As a lower-alcohol, softer-hitting cocktail recipe, this combination of Amaro Montenegro and fino sherry is a Spain vs.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients except soda water to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
3. Top with soda and garnish with a half orange wheel.

second-serve-2.descEn: As a lower-alcohol, softer-hitting cocktail recipe, this combination of Amaro Montenegro and fino sherry is a Spain vs.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients except soda water to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
3. Top with soda and garnish with a half orange wheel.

see-you-on-wednesday.descEn: This zero-proof Spicy Margarita variation from Natasha David combines celery juice, lime juice, jalapeno, cilantro, agave nectar, and salt.
stepsEn: 1. At the bottom of a shaker, muddle the jalapeño, cilantro, and agave nectar.
2. Add the celery juice, lime juice, and salt solution. Add ice and shake until well chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a Tajín-rimmed double rocks glass over large-format ice.

seelbach.descEn: The Seelbach Cocktail may not be a julep, but it doesn't have to be: it's respectable, powerful, and delicious right down to the bottom of the glass.
stepsEn: 1. Add the bourbon, Cointreau, Angostura bitters and Peychaud’s bitters into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled flute.
3. Top with cold Champagne or other sparkling wine.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.

sentimental-gentleman.descEn: Two Sundays ago, Andrea and I ate dinner at Veggie Galaxy and headed over to Brick and Mortar where bartenders Kenny Belanger and Misty Kalkofen were making drinks.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all ingredients.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.

seven-seas-swizzle.descEn: In his recipe, Nick Batavia plays with green tea syrup and lime, for a riff on the Queen Park Swizzle with traditional punch ingredients.
stepsEn: 1. Build all the ingredients in the appropriate glass and add half the amount of necessary ice.
2. Swizzle until the glass is cool.
3. Top with ice and garnish.
seven-seas-swizzle.garnishEn: Mint bouquet and dusting of nutmeg

sex-on-the-beach.descEn: There are two general types of the cocktail: - The IBA official cocktail is made from vodka, peach schnapps, orange juice, and cranberry juice.
stepsEn: Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
sex-on-the-beach.garnishEn: Garnish with a half orange slice.

sex-work-is-real-work.descEn: Christine Wiseman's cocktail recipe is a take on the frozen Pornstar Martini with additions of umami-forward umeboshi and Champagne acid.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a blender.
2. Blend until smooth and serve in your glass of choice.
3. Garnish with edible flower and mint bouquet.

shade-thrower.descEn: For a less bitter and smoother Boulevardier riff, Freddy Schwenk of Geist in Nashville swapped out the Campari with Averna and Aperol.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a glass filled with a large ice cube, and garnish.

shannon-tebays-paloma.descEn: Coming in on top in our Paloma tasting was this cocktail by Shannon Tebay of Death & Co.
stepsEn: 1. Salt the rim of the Collins glass, then add the Topo Chico and set aside.
2. Combine all the remaining ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the Collins glass, add ice, and garnish with a lime wedge.

shirley-temple.descEn: The cocktail may have been invented by a bartender at Chasen's, a restaurant in West Hollywood, California, to serve then-child actress Shirley Temple.
stepsEn: 1. Fill a Collins glass with cubed ice.
2. Add the grenadine and lime juice.
3. Top with the ginger ale and gently stir to combine.
shirley-temple.garnishEn: Garnish with two skewered Luxardo maraschino cherries.

stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to shaker

## Editors note:
This may seem a stiff pour, but in maceration the juiced hulls will actually soak up a significant cut of the gin—up to 3/4 ounce—and can leave the drink wan if not fortified a touch.

tom-macys-gimlet.descEn: Tom Macy's Gimlet cocktail recipe is simple: two ounces of gin, three-quarters of an ounce of simple syrup and half an ounce of lime juice.
stepsEn: 1. Cut a lime in half, then cut one half into quarters.
2. Muddle the limes in simple syrup.
3. Add lime juice and gin.
4. Shake and fine strain into a coupe.

tommys-margarita.descEn: Tommy's margarita was conceived in San Francisco in 1990 by Julio Bermejo at his parents' restaurant called Tommy's (not to be confused with Tommy's Place in Juárez, Mexico.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with ice.

tonic-rickey.descEn: This simple non-alcoholic Tonic Rickey from cocktail blogger Camille Wilson combines lime juice, simple syrup, tonic water, seltzer water, and Angostura bitters.
stepsEn: 1. In a lowball glass filled with ice, add the lime juice and simple syrup. Stir to combine.
2. Slowly stir in the tonic water and seltzer water.
3. Top with the bitters and serve.

tonico-di-corte.descEn: Put a little dinamismo in your G&T!
stepsEn: 1. Add tonic, Italicus, and gin to a highball glass filled with ice
2. Top with soda water and stir

toronto.descEn: This flavorful Toronto cocktail combines the depth and warmth of whiskey with the intrigue of herbal Fernet-Branca liqueur.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the rye whiskey, Fernet-Branca, syrup and bitters in a cocktail mixing glass (or any other type of glass).
2. Fill the mixing glass with 1 handful ice and stir continuously for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a glass.
toronto.garnishEn: Garnish with an orange peel and serve.

trader-vics-sour.descEn: Trader Vic created countless variations on the sour.
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker, add all ingredients
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Strain over fresh ice into an old fashioned glass
trader-vics-sour.garnishEn: Garnish with a lemon wheel and an orchid

tradewinds-negroni.descEn: Justin Elliott of The Townsend in Austin created this spicy variation on the Negroni using equal parts sweet vermouth, Cointreau, and Angostura bitters.
stepsEn: Add sweet vermouth, Cointreau, and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass and fill with ice. Stir until well chilled, about 25 seconds. Strain into an Old Fashioned glass with a large ice cube. Express orange oils from twist over drink, garnish with twist, and serve.

trasatlantico-fizz.descEn: World-renowned bar and Imbibe 75 Place to Watch, Florería Atlántico in Buenos Aires, combines winter citrus in a bright and easy-drinking gin fizz.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all of the ingredients, except the club soda, in a shaker and shake hard for 10 seconds without ice.
2. Add ice and shake again for another 10 seconds.
3. Strain into a glass over ice and top with club soda.
4. Garnish.
trasatlantico-fizz.garnishEn: Orange wedge and spritz of peated scotch

treacle.descEn: One of the simplest of Bradsell’s inventions to have found lasting popularity, this is an Old-Fashioned variation.
stepsEn: 1. Build in a double rocks glass filled with ice.
2. Float cloudy apple juice on top.

trinidad-sour.descEn: Unusually for a cocktail, it uses Angostura bitters as a base spirit rather than as a flavoring, the bitters being the single largest component of the drink in its IBA formulation.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker
2. Shake well with ice
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

tropical-popsicle.descEn: A Japanese Whisky collins, with acidity, bitter notes and tropical flavors for a pop!
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients, except soda water, to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with cubed ice
4. Top with club soda

tropical-storm.descEn: Passionfruit Syrup and dark rum shine in this daiquiri-hurricane hybrid.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled glass

truly-scrumptious.descEn: Pear eau de vie and unaged South American grape brandy combine their fragrant forces in this luscious cocktail.
stepsEn: Shake all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a glass holding a single large ice cube. Garnish.

tunnel.descEn: This recipe for the Tunnel is a Negroni-like drink from Paris bar Cravan.
stepsEn: 1. Stir all ingredients until chilled in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Strain into a coupe.

turf-club.descEn: This Martini variation is a complex rendition of the classic made with absinthe and maraschino liqueur.
stepsEn: 1. Add the gin, dry vermouth, maraschino, absinthe, and bitters into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

tuxedo.descEn: Related to the martini, the Tuxedo has had many variations since its inception in the 1880s.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into chilled martini cocktail glass.
tuxedo.garnishEn: Garnish with cherry and lemon zest

twelve-mile-limit.descEn: During the 18th century the US territorial waters were limited to 3 nautical miles.
stepsEn: 1. In a cocktail shaker, add all the ingredients
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe
4. Garnish with a twist of lemon

ultima-palabra.descEn: Named after the direct Spanish translation of Last Word, hence the use of mezcal in place of the gin in a classic Last Word cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass

ume-paloma.descEn: The Ume Paloma is a highball cocktail recipe combining blanco tequila, umeshu, pink grapefruit juice, lime juice and club soda.
stepsEn: 1. If using, rim a highball glass with sea salt.
2. Fill the glass with ice cubes.
3. Add the club soda first, then the other ingredients.
4. Stir gently to blend.

valkyrie.descEn: After the Snake in the Grass at Temple Bar, bartender Sam Gabrielli wanted to showcase a drink he created called the Valkyrie.
stepsEn: Stir with ice and strain into a rocks glass.
valkyrie.garnishEn: Twist a grapefruit peel over the top and discard

vento.descEn: The Ve.n.to is one of the new additions to the IBA (International Bartender Association) cocktail list.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into the shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled small tumbler glass filled with ice.
Notes:
If desired water can be replaced by chamomile infusion in the honey mix.
vento.garnishEn: Garnish with lemon zest and white grapes.

verte-chaud.descEn: An après-ski staple perfect for the chilly chartreuse fan
stepsEn: 1. Stir together hot water and shaved chocolate until combined
2. Add Chartreuse and top with wet cream

vesper.descEn: The Vesper or Vesper Martini is a cocktail that was originally made of gin, vodka, and Kina Lillet.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice cubes. Shake and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

vieille-place.descEn: A twist on the classic Vieux Carré, the Vieille Place is a balanced, yet spirit-forward, bittersweet aperitif.
stepsEn: Stir all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass

vieux-carre.descEn: It originated with Walter Bergeron, a bartender at New Orleans’ Carousel Bar in the Hotel Monteleone.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
vieux-carre.garnishEn: Garnish with orange zest and maraschino cherry.

vitamin-parade.descEn: Natasha David combines fresh carrot and pineapple juices, citrus, ginger beer, and cinnamon syrup for this feel-good spirit-free drink.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the carrot juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, syrup, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Dry-shake with no ice for 15–20 seconds until foam forms.
3. Add ice and shake. Fine-strain into a fizz glass.
4. Top with ginger beer.
5. Express a lemon twist over cocktail then discard.

ward-eight.descEn: The Ward Eight cocktail is a relative of the Whiskey Sour and thought to have been invented at Boston’s Locke-Ober Café in 1898.
stepsEn: Shake ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass. Add an ice cube and a splash of sparkling water.
1. Stir with ice.
2. Strain into a cocktail glass.

washingtons-mule.descEn: An autumnal and all-American version of the Moscow Mule.
stepsEn: 1. Combine syrup, brandy, lime juice, and bitters with ice in a cocktail shaker for a short shake.
2. Strain over ice into a highball glass.
3. Top with soda water and stir.

whiskey-apple-highball.descEn: It isn’t plausible to say one bar invented such a simple highball.
stepsEn: 1. Build in a highball filled with ice.
2. Stir.

whiskey-business.descEn: The Whiskey Business cocktail recipe is Meaghan Dorman's spicy riff on a Whiskey Sour featuring chile liqueur and cinnamon syrup.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a glass over a ice.
3. Garnish with lemon wheel dusted in ancho chile powder.
whiskey-business.garnishEn: lemon wheel dusted in ancho chile powder

whiskey-peach-smash.descEn: A riff on the OG Whiskey Smash, Dale DeGroff's Whiskey Peach Smash recipe adds fresh fruit and citrus to energize the classic formula.
stepsEn: 1. Muddle the fruit and lemon wedges with the Curaçao.
2. Add the mint leaves and the bourbon.
3. Shake well and strain into a double rocks glass filled with ice.
whiskey-peach-smash.garnishEn: Garnish with a peach slice and a mint sprig

whiskey-smash.descEn: A riff on the Mint Julep, the Whiskey Smash cocktail recipe features lemon and mint, making it a potent number dangerously easy to toss back.
stepsEn: 1. In a rocks glass, gently muddle mint with simple syrup to release oils.
2. Add lemon pieces and muddle to release juice.
3. Add crushed ice or small ice cubes and pour bourbon over.
4. Swizzle gently to mix.
5. Garnish with a mint spring and lemon wheel.

whiskey-sour.descEn: The oldest historical mention of a whiskey sour was published in the Wisconsin newspaper, Waukesha Plain Dealer, in 1870.
stepsEn: 1. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake well.
3. Strain into cobbler glass.
4. If served “On the rocks”, strain ingredients into an old fashioned glass filled with ice.
NOTE:
If egg white is used shake little harder to release and incorporate the foam from the egg white.
whiskey-sour.garnishEn: Garnish with a half orange slice and maraschino cherry, optionally use orange zest.

whisky-highball.descEn: Initially, the most common highball was made with Scotch whisky and carbonated water, known simply as a "Scotch and soda".
stepsEn: 1. Cut a lemon ready for garnishing and squeezing
2. Fill your highball with ice
3. Pour all the ingredients into your glass
4. Top up with soda water
5. Stir the drink gently together, mixing all the ingredients
6. Garnish with the lemon wedge

white-lady.descEn: It was first created in 1919 in London by Harry MacElhone and it was equal parts creme de menthe, triple sec and lemon juice.
stepsEn: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

white-mezcal-negroni.descEn: This White Negroni cocktail recipe swaps gin for mezcal and the expected Suze for Domaine La Bohème Gentiane Extra Bitter Aperitif.
stepsEn: 1. Combine in a mixing glass with ice and stir briefly for five seconds.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube or whatever ice you have.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist expressed over the drink, then discarded.

white-negroni.descEn: The White Negroni is a fabulous use of the gentian's powers, and a downright brilliant twist on a bonafide classic.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients with ice and stir
2. Strain into a lowball glass

white-negroni-corpse-revived.descEn: We went nearly a century before a handful of rowdy boozehounds in NYC decided the Negroni needed more gin and less of everything else, but it took less than a decade for those same bartenders to tinker with Collins' White Negroni.
stepsEn: Build in glass over ice

white-negroni-sbagliato.descEn: This White Negroni Sbagliato recipe by Brooklyn's Long Island Bar mixes herbal Suze and bianco vermouth for a summer to fall spritz.
stepsEn: 1. Build over a large cube in a double Old-Fashioned glass.
2. Garnish with a long slice of cucumber and a twist of orange zest.

white-russian.descEn: Misleadingly, this sophisticated cocktail is not in fact Russian in origin, but gets its name from vodka being the base spirit.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the vodka, coffee liqueur and ice cubes in a cocktail shaker
2. Shake well and strain into an ice-filled short tumbler
3. Lightly beat the single cream until just frothy and pour onto the drink over the back of a spoon, to help make it float

white-russian-gus-sip-and-dip.descEn: Fans of the White Russian will love this richer, creamier take on the classic coffee cocktail.
stepsEn: 1. Put a glass in the freezer for at least 30 minutes before preparing the cocktail. Combine the vodka, coffee liqueur, coffee, and vanilla syrup with ice and shake to chill, then set aside.

2. Fill the chilled glass with large ice cubes. Add the foam cream to the bottom of the glass over ice, filling a 1/3 of the glass. Carefully pour the prepared cocktail base over the foam cream for a rich, layered presentation.
3. Foam CreamCombine 8 parts of heavy cream with 1 part of simple syrup (1:1)  in a shaker. Shake until thickened but still pourable.

whitechapel-gt.descEn: While developing a Gin & Tonic menu for gin-focused bar Whitechapel, co-owner and beverage director Alex Smith looked to Italian flavors for inspiration—and wound up with a hybrid that evokes another gin-based classic.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the first 3 ingredients in an ice-filled highball glass and top with chilled tonic, to taste; stir to combine, then garnish.

wildest-redhead.descEn: This easy whiskey cocktail recipe combines blended Scotch whisky, allspice or pimento dram, Cherry Heering, lemon and honey syrup.
stepsEn: 1. Add the first four ingredients to a shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain over a large ice cube into a rocks glass.
3. Slowly pour the Cherry Heering over the ice so that it sinks to the bottom of the drink.
Shake

winterized-negroni.descEn: A half-teaspoon of Islay Scotch brings robust and malty flavors to the Negroni for a winterized take on the aperitivo classic.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a coupe glass.

wisconsin-old-fashioned.descEn: The Wisconsin Old Fashioned is the state’s variation on the classic Old Fashioned cocktail, with brandy and lemon lime soda.
stepsEn: 1. In a chilled old fashioned glass, muddle the sugar, bitters, orange wedge and cherry into a thick paste, careful not to overwork the orange peel.
2. Add brandy or Cognac and stir.
3. Fill glass with crushed ice and serve.

wiz-fizz.descEn: In this fizzy cocktail recipe, gin, Cynar, lemon, and vanilla syrup act as a base, while egg white and heavy cream combine for a rich body.
stepsEn: 1. Fill a highball glass 1/5 full with root beer and set aside.
2. Combine the remaining ingredients, except the cream, in a mixing tin and dry shake without ice.
3. Add the cream and dry shake again.
4. Add ice and shake again for 30 to 40 seconds.
5. Strain the ice out of the shaker and dry shake once more for 1 minute.
6. Pour the contents of the shaker into the highball glass and allow to settle before adding a final topper.
wiz-fizz.garnishEn: Garnish with grated nutmeg and a straw.

wray-and-ting.descEn: Wray and Ting is a simple highball cocktail made with delicious overproof Jamaican rum and a refreshing grapefruit soda.
stepsEn: 1. Add ice to a collins glass.
2. Measure in the rum.
3. Top with Ting and garnish if you'd like.

yellow.descEn: The Yellow is a cocktail recipe combining London dry gin, yellow Chartreuse, Suze and lemon juice in a Last Word-like drink.
stepsEn: 1. Combine the ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Double-strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
3. Express the lemon twists over the surface of the drink and discard.
Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.

your-mothers-spritz.descEn: The white wine spritzer, popularized by "ladies who lunch" during the '50s, gets reimagined through a modern lens.
stepsEn: 1. Add the ingredients, except the grapefruit soda, to a wine glass over ice. Top with the soda. Garnish.

yuzu-negroni.descEn: At Hong Kong's Bar Leone (named 50 Best Bars' best bar in Asia and Spirited Awards' Best International Bar) the yuzu Negroni is one of the most ordered cocktails.
stepsEn: 1. Add all the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice. Stir to chill and strain into the glass over a large ice cube. Express with a lemon peel and garnish.

zombie.descEn: It first appeared in late 1934, invented by Donn Beach at his Hollywood Don the Beachcomber restaurant.
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients into an electric blender with 170 grams of cracked ice.
2. With pulse bottom blend for a few seconds.
3. Serve in a tall tumbler glass.
Donn’s Mix: 2 parts of fresh yellow grapefruit and 1 part of cinnamon syrup

zombie-apocalypse.descEn: A spooky, autumnal zombie riff that's perfect for a Halloween night!
stepsEn: 1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add a small amount of ice and shake until chilled
3. Strain over crushed ice into a chilled glass

zombie-spritz.descEn: At Dante's, this low-ABV spritz tangles with the Zombie's famously layered build for a cocktail recipe that feels firmly rooted to both.
stepsEn: 1. Combine all ingredients, except the Cava rosé, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a goblet or tiki mug over crushed ice
3. Top with cava rosé.
zombie-spritz.garnishEn: dehydrated grapefruit slice, fresh mint, cocktail umbrella (optional)

strukani-pelin.descEn: Štrukani pelinkovac (or štrukani pelin) is a somewhat novel Croatian drink that combines pelinkovac (traditional herbal liqueur) with lemon juice.
stepsEn: 1. A lemon slice is then squeezed directly into the glass and mixed.
The amount of lemon juice can vary, sometimes resulting in a drink with equal amounts of both ingredients. More elaborate versions often add orange juice, citrus zest, or spices.
